scenario: Ticketmaster 白板面试只有 45 分钟，功能清单必须砍到能当场讲完主链路的最小集合。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes on the whiteboard for Ticketmaster, so the feature list has to shrink to what you can actually design end to end.
q: Ticketmaster 设计中被排进「核心功能需求」的前三条是？
q_en: Which three requirements are in scope for the Ticketmaster core design?
options: 查看活动、搜索活动、订票
查看已订活动、管理员建活动、动态定价
支付、退款、转赠门票
注册登录、个人资料、消息通知
why: 决定性因素是 45 分钟的时间预算：只锁定查看、搜索、订票三条才能让设计聚焦执行。
why_en: The three core requirements are view, search, and book because a time-boxed interview needs a tight, executable scope.
options_en: View events, search events, and book tickets.
View booked events, let admins add events, and dynamic pricing.
Handle payments, refunds, and ticket gifting.
Registration and login, profile, and notifications.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试方法论里指明确排除在本轮设计范围之外、但值得一提的功能点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Below the line marks a feature you explicitly scope out of the current design but still mention for credit.

optionExplanations: 查看、搜索、订票正是原文圈定的核心三条，用它们撑起 45 分钟里能讲完的 MVP。
这三项原文标为 below the line：产品价值高但不是本轮必答项，讲了会挤占核心时间。
支付/退款/转赠属于订票后的售后环节，不在功能需求的核心三条里。
注册登录、资料、通知是通用账户功能，不是订票平台独有的核心决策点。
optionExplanations_en: View, search, and book are exactly the article's core three — enough to fill a 45-minute MVP without sprawling.
These are marked below the line: valuable but not required this round, so covering them eats into core time.
Payment, refunds, and gifting are post-booking add-ons, not part of the core three requirements.
Login, profile, and notifications are generic account features, not decisions unique to a ticketing platform.

scenario: 开售瞬间百万人刷同一个活动页，而同一张票绝对不能卖给两个人。
scenario_en: At on-sale a million people refresh the same event page, and the one thing you can never do is sell the same seat twice.
q: Ticketmaster 在一致性/可用性上的取舍是？
q_en: What consistency-versus-availability tradeoff does Ticketmaster make?
options: 无论读还是写，全系统统一使用强一致模型
无论读还是写，全系统统一优先可用性
查看/搜索优先可用性，订票优先一致性防双重预订
订票也用最终一致，靠异步对账事后纠正双重预订
why: 决定性约束是读写路径的重要性不同：查看/搜索要扛峰值流量，订票必须防止同一张票卖两次。
why_en: The system splits CAP by path: view and search favor availability under peak traffic, while booking favors consistency to prevent double booking.
options_en: Whether reading or writing, the whole system uses one strong-consistency model.
Whether reading or writing, the whole system prioritizes availability.
View/search favor availability; booking favors consistency to stop double booking.
Booking uses eventual consistency too, fixing any double bookings afterward via async reconciliation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任何时刻的读操作都能看到最新一次成功写入的结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means every read immediately reflects the latest successful write.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许短暂的数据不一致，只保证经过一段时间后各副本会收敛到同一个值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency allows brief staleness but guarantees replicas converge to the same value over time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一张票被两个不同用户同时买走的错误场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Double booking is when two different users end up purchasing the same ticket at once.

optionExplanations: 全系统统一强一致会把查看/搜索也拖进锁等待，浪费本该扛峰值的读吞吐。
全系统统一优先可用性会让订票路径也能接受短暂不一致，出现双重预订。
查看/搜索优先可用性扛峰值流量，订票靠事务保一致防止同一张票卖两次，读写各取所需。
订票用最终一致时，两人可能同时把同一张票标为已订；异步对账只能事后退款道歉，防不住双订真正发生。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing strong consistency everywhere drags view/search into lock waits, wasting read throughput needed for spikes.
Prioritizing availability everywhere lets the booking path tolerate staleness too, opening the door to double-booking.
View/search lean on availability to absorb peak traffic, while booking uses transactions for consistency so a seat can't sell twice — each path gets what it needs.
With eventual consistency on booking, two users can mark the same seat booked at once; async reconciliation only refunds after the fact — it can't prevent the double sale.

scenario: 面试官已经确认查看/搜索优先可用性、订票优先一致性；你量化出热门活动 1000 万用户抢票、搜索低于 500ms、读写比约 100:1。
scenario_en: The interviewer confirms view/search favors availability while booking favors consistency; you quantify hot events at ten million competing users, search under 500ms, and roughly a 100:1 read/write ratio.
q: 这些非功能数字最支持哪些设计判断？
q_en: Which design decisions do these non-functional numbers support?
why: 这三个数字定后续方向：并发峰值→排队与缓存；延迟上限→搜索索引；读写比→缓存与横向扩展读路径。
why_en: These three numbers drive every later design choice: concurrency sets up queuing, the latency cap sets up search indexing, and the read ratio sets up caching.
text: 并发峰值推动{{排队与缓存}}；500ms 延迟上限推动{{搜索索引}}；100:1 读写比推动{{读路径缓存与横向扩展}}。

scenario: Ticketmaster 是读多写少系统，读写比约 100:1（每 100 次查看/搜索对应 1 次订票）。
scenario_en: Ticketmaster is read-heavy: about 100 view or search requests for every booking write.
q: 「读写比 100:1」这个数字直接推导出的架构含义是？
q_en: What architecture implication follows from the 100:1 read-write ratio?
options: 系统写多，需要针对写入优化的存储引擎
读多写少，要靠缓存和横向扩展撑住读路径
读写均衡，无需特殊处理
应该砍掉搜索功能
why: 100 次读换 1 次写，说明负载几乎全在查看/搜索路径，缓存和横向扩展要优先砸在读路径上。
why_en: A 100-to-1 read-write ratio means almost all load sits on the read path, so caching and horizontal scaling should target reads first.
options_en: The system is write-heavy and needs a write-optimized storage engine.
The system is read-heavy and must lean on caching and horizontal read scaling.
Reads and writes are balanced, so no special handling is needed.
The system should drop the search feature.
optionExplanations: 把 100:1 读写比读反了——负载几乎全在读路径，不是写路径需要优化的存储引擎。
100 次读换 1 次写说明负载几乎全压在查看/搜索，缓存和横向扩展要优先砸向读路径。
100:1 明显是读远多于写，不是均衡负载，跳过特殊处理会让读路径先扛不住。
读写比高只说明该往读路径投入资源，不是砍掉产生读流量的搜索功能本身。
optionExplanations_en: This flips the 100:1 ratio backward — the load sits almost entirely on reads, not a write path needing a specialized engine.
100 reads per write means the load is almost all on view/search, so cache and horizontal scaling should target the read path first.
A 100:1 ratio is heavily read-skewed, not balanced — skipping special handling means the read path buckles first.
A high read:write ratio says invest in the read path, not cut the search feature that generates those reads.

scenario: 45 分钟的面试里，能想到的功能点远超时间允许，需要决定讲什么。
scenario_en: In a 45-minute interview, there are more possible features than time, so you must choose what to cover.
q: 对功能需求列表的正确处理方式是？
q_en: How should you handle the functional requirement list?
options: 把所有能想到的功能都一股脑塞进设计里，逐条平均展开，完全不做取舍
只挑自己最熟悉、最擅长讲的那部分功能来说，其余绝口不提
完全跳过需求梳理这一步，需求都没理清就直接画架构图
只留 top 3 核心功能，其余标为 below the line
why: 只选 top 3 才能在有限时间里聚焦执行；below the line 顺带展示产品思维。
why_en: Picking only the top three keeps execution focused within the time limit, while noting the rest below the line still shows product thinking.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确要求补上某个 below the line 功能（如管理员建活动），就把它提到线上一起设计。
tradeoff: 执行聚焦度 vs 需求覆盖广度
options_en: Cram every feature you can think of into the design, walking through each one evenly, with zero prioritization.
Only cover the features you personally know best and are most comfortable presenting, and skip the rest entirely.
Skip the requirements pass entirely and start sketching the architecture before anything is scoped.
Keep only the top 3 core features and label everything else below the line.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试方法论里指明确排除在本轮设计范围之外、但值得一提的功能点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Below the line marks a feature you explicitly scope out of the current design but still mention for credit.

optionExplanations: 45 分钟塞不下所有功能还逐条平均展开，只会做得又浅又乱——只有时间完全不设限时才行得通。
按个人熟悉度取舍会让面试官觉得需求判断被喜好代替，除非面试官明确只考察你最强的那块。
跳过需求梳理会让面试官追问依据，反而拖慢后面设计——只有需求已经提前对齐时才能省这一步。
只留 top 3、其余标 below the line 既能在有限时间里聚焦执行，也留出让面试官调整优先级的机会。
optionExplanations_en: 45 minutes can't fit every feature walked through evenly; it just goes shallow and messy — only works if time is truly unlimited.
Picking by personal comfort reads as preference over judgment, unless the interviewer explicitly wants your strongest area only.
Skipping requirements invites the interviewer to ask for the reasoning anyway, slowing things down — only skip if scope is already agreed.
Keeping the top 3 and labeling the rest below the line focuses execution time while leaving room for the interviewer to redirect priorities.

scenario: 要为 Ticketmaster 画数据模型，只画支撑查看、搜索、订票三条主链路的最小实体集。
scenario_en: You're drawing Ticketmaster's data model, keeping only the entities that the view, search, and book paths actually need.
q: Ticketmaster 的核心实体包含哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which entities belong in Ticketmaster's core model?
options: Event、User、Performer
Venue、Ticket、Booking
ShoppingCart（购物车）
SeatLock（座位锁表）
why: 六个核心实体覆盖活动、账户、场馆和交易四类信息；购物车和锁票表都不在这份清单里。
why_en: The six core entities are Event, User, Performer, Venue, Ticket, and Booking - there is no shopping cart or seat-lock entity.
options_en: Event, User, and Performer.
Venue, Ticket, and Booking.
ShoppingCart (a shopping-cart entity).
SeatLock (a seat-lock table).
optionExplanations: Event、User、Performer 是覆盖活动与账户信息的三个基础实体。
Venue、Ticket、Booking 补上场馆与交易信息，六个实体一起构成完整模型。
购物车是电商场景常见实体，本设计没有把它列进核心实体清单。
座位锁表属于后面并发控制的候选方案，那里靠条件写/版本校验兜底正确性，不进这份实体清单。
optionExplanations_en: Event, User, and Performer are the three base entities covering event and account information.
Venue, Ticket, and Booking add venue and transaction data, completing the six-entity model.
A shopping cart is a common e-commerce entity, but it isn't on this design's core entity list.
A seat-lock table belongs to the later concurrency candidates, where a conditional write with a version check guards correctness — not to this entity list.

scenario: 一个场馆一年办 200 场演出，座位布局固定不变，不能每场活动各存一份座位图。
scenario_en: A venue hosts 200 shows a year with a fixed seating layout, so you cannot duplicate the seat map per event.
q: 座位图（seat map）数据存在哪个实体里？
q_en: Which entity should own the seat map data?
options: Venue：JSON 或关联表存区/排/座位号及坐标
Ticket：给每张票都各存一份含坐标的完整座位图
Event：给每场活动重复存一份座位图
Booking：把座位图记在订单信息里
why: 座位图描述的是场馆的物理布局，属于 Venue；活动、票、订单都不该各自重复存一份。
why_en: The seat map describes the venue's physical layout, so it belongs on Venue rather than being duplicated per event, ticket, or booking.
options_en: Venue: JSON or a related table with section, row, seat number, and coordinates.
Ticket: every ticket stores its own full copy of the seat map, coordinates included.
Event: each event stores a duplicate copy of the seat map.
Booking: the seat map is recorded on the order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述场馆分区、排、座位号及坐标的数据结构，用来渲染可交互选座界面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A seat map is the data structure describing a venue's sections, rows, and seat numbers used to render an interactive seat picker.

optionExplanations: 座位图是场馆的物理布局，存在 Venue 里，同一场馆的多场活动能直接复用。
把座位图连坐标一起存进每张 Ticket，会让同一场馆的座位图被冗余复制成千上万份。
把座位图挂在 Event 上会导致同一场馆办多场活动时重复存好几份。
把座位图记进 Booking 会让它在订单结束后失去归属，场馆信息不该绑在交易记录上。
optionExplanations_en: The seat map is the venue's physical layout, so it lives on Venue — every event there can reuse the same map.
Storing the full coordinate seat map per Ticket duplicates the same map across thousands of ticket rows.
Attaching it to Event means the same venue's multiple events each re-store the same map.
Storing it on Booking leaves the map orphaned once the order closes — venue data shouldn't live on a transaction record.

scenario: 一场演出 6 万个座位，订票必须在一次短事务里把某个座位改成已售。
scenario_en: A show has 60,000 seats, and booking has to flip one specific seat to sold inside a single short transaction.
q: 新活动创建时，Ticket 记录是怎么产生的？
q_en: How are Ticket rows created when a new event is added?
options: 用户第一次点击座位时系统才临时创建
创建活动时按座位图批量预生成门票
支付成功后由 Stripe 统一创建
只给 VIP 座位预先创建门票
why: 座位图上的每个座位在活动创建时就要有一行 Ticket 记录，订票就变成对一行状态的更新。
why_en: Every seat on the venue's seat map gets a ticket row at event creation, so booking becomes a simple status update on that row.
options_en: Created on the fly the first time a user clicks a seat.
One ticket per seat is batch pre-generated from the seat map at event creation.
Stripe creates the ticket after payment succeeds.
Tickets are pre-created only for VIP seats.
optionExplanations: 点击才临时创建票据在并发下容易缺失或重复创建，撑不住抢票场景。
活动创建时按座位图批量预生成 Ticket，订票就变成对一行已有状态的更新，而不是现造一行。
把票据创建职责交给支付服务商 Stripe 放错了层——它只该负责收款，不该管库存记录。
只给 VIP 预建票会让普通座位无票可订，座位图也没法完整渲染。
optionExplanations_en: Creating a ticket row on first click is prone to missing or duplicate rows under concurrency — it won't survive a ticket rush.
Batch-pregenerating Ticket rows from the seat map at event creation turns booking into updating a row, not creating one.
Handing ticket creation to Stripe puts it at the wrong layer — Stripe should only handle payment, not inventory records.
Pregenerating only VIP tickets leaves regular seats with no ticket row, so the seat map can't render fully.

scenario: 用户常一次买 4 张连座票：一笔支付、一个总价、退款也是整单退。
scenario_en: People usually buy four seats together — one payment, one total price, and refunds happen for the whole order.
q: 为什么要单独建 Booking 实体，而不是把订单信息折进 Ticket？
q_en: Why model Booking separately instead of folding order data into Ticket?
options: 受限于 Ticket 表的列数上限
为满足微服务「一服务一库」原则
多票订单需要共享总价和支付状态
是为了满足 GDPR 合规要求
why: 一次交易常常买多张票，Booking 把它们聚合成一个订单，共享总价和支付状态。
why_en: A single purchase often covers multiple tickets, so Booking groups them into one order that shares a total price and payment status.
options_en: Limited by the Ticket table's column count.
To satisfy the microservice rule of one database per service.
A multi-ticket order needs a shared total price and payment status.
To satisfy GDPR compliance requirements.

termDefinitions.meaning: 欧盟颁布的通用数据保护条例，规范用户数据的收集与使用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GDPR is the EU regulation that governs how companies collect and handle user data.

optionExplanations: 把建模决定归因到 Ticket 表列数上限没有依据，列数从来不是这里的约束。
「一服务一库」是微服务通用原则，但不是这题拆出 Booking 实体的真正原因。
一次结账常常包含好几张票，需要一个实体把它们捆成一单，统一算总价、统一追支付状态。
GDPR 是数据隐私合规范畴，跟要不要单独建 Booking 实体没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Blaming it on a column-count limit on Ticket has no basis — that was never the real constraint here.
"One service, one database" is a general microservices principle, but it isn't the actual reason Booking was split out here.
A single checkout often bundles several tickets, so something has to group them into one order with one shared total and one payment status.
GDPR is a data-privacy compliance concern, unrelated to whether Booking needs its own entity.

scenario: 订票事务只锁一行 Ticket，就要判断出它属于哪场、哪个座位、多少钱、是否已售。
scenario_en: The booking transaction touches a single ticket row, so that row alone must tell you the event, the seat, the price, and whether it is sold.
q: Ticket 表包含哪些关键字段？
q_en: What key fields belong on the Ticket table?
options: 只记录座位号和价格，别的字段一概没有
记录用户密码和支付卡号这类账户敏感信息
记录场馆地址、场馆总容量、停车信息这类场馆级字段
eventId、座位、价格、状态、bookingId
why: Ticket 要能独立判断归属哪场活动、哪个座位、多少钱、是否已售，还要能挂回 Booking。
why_en: A ticket row needs enough fields to stand alone: which event, which seat, its price, its status, and a link back to its booking.
options_en: Only seat number and price, with no other fields at all.
User password and payment card number, which are account-level sensitive data.
Venue address, total capacity, and parking info — venue-level fields.
eventId, seat, price, status, and bookingId.
optionExplanations: 只记录座位号和价格缺了 eventId 和状态，票无法关联活动，也判断不了能不能卖。
密码、卡号是完全不同安全边界的账户/支付数据，不该混进票据表。
场馆地址、总容量、停车信息都属于 Venue 级字段，不该重复存进每一张票。
eventId、座位、价格、状态、bookingId 齐全后，一张票就能独立判断归属、价格与可购状态，还能挂回订单。
optionExplanations_en: Storing only seat and price misses eventId and status, so a ticket can't tell which event it belongs to or if it's sellable.
Passwords and card numbers sit in a completely different trust boundary — they don't belong on a ticket row.
Venue address, total capacity, and parking are venue-level fields; repeating them on every ticket row is redundant.
With eventId, seat, price, status, and bookingId, a ticket can independently tell its event, price, status, and link back to an order.

q: 补全实体之间的关系：
q_en: Fill in the relationships between the entities.
why: 座位图先由 Venue 定义，活动创建时批量生成 Ticket，下单时 Booking 聚合多张票并回填 bookingId。
why_en: The seat map lives on the venue, tickets are pre-generated per event, and a booking groups the purchased tickets and writes back their bookingId.
text: Ticket 通过 {{bookingId}} 列关联到 Booking；新活动创建时按 Venue 的 {{座位图}} 给每个座位生成一张票；客户端用座位图加每张票的 {{状态}} 渲染可交互选座界面。

scenario: 活动详情页要在客户端直接渲染可交互座位图，用户点开就能看出哪些座位还能选。
scenario_en: The event page renders an interactive seat map on the client, so a user can see at a glance which seats are still selectable.
q: GET /events/:eventId 除了返回 Event、Venue、Performer，为什么还要带 Ticket[]？
q_en: Why should GET /events/:eventId include Ticket[] along with Event, Venue, and Performer?
options: 为了让客户端把所有票据都缓存下来
客户端需要用每张票的状态在座位图上渲染可选/已售座位
为了做订票前的支付预授权检查
REST 规范硬性要求响应必须一次返回全部关联实体
why: 详情页的核心是可交互座位图，客户端要靠每张票的状态才能画出哪些座位可选、哪些已售。
why_en: The event page's core feature is an interactive seat map, so the client needs each ticket's status to know which seats are open.
options_en: So the client can cache every ticket record it gets back.
The client needs each ticket's status to render available/sold seats on the seat map.
So the client can run a payment pre-authorization check before booking.
The REST spec strictly requires every response to return all related entities at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种基于 HTTP 动词和资源路径设计 API 的架构风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that models resources with URLs and standard HTTP verbs like GET and POST.

optionExplanations: 缓存不是这里的目的——客户端需要的是实时座位状态，不是把票据囤起来。
座位图要能交互点选，前端得知道每个座位当前是空的还是已售，这份状态就来自票据数组。
支付预授权发生在订票流程里，跟查看活动详情时要不要带票据数组无关。
REST 规范并不强制一次返回全部关联实体，返回票据数组只是为了满足座位图渲染的具体需求。
optionExplanations_en: Caching isn't the goal here — the client needs live seat status, not a stash of ticket records.
The seat map has to be clickable, so the frontend needs to know which seats are open versus taken, and that comes straight from the ticket array.
Payment pre-authorization happens during booking, unrelated to whether event-detail responses include the ticket array.
REST doesn't mandate returning every related entity at once — the ticket array is included only to serve seat-map rendering.

scenario: 用户按关键词、日期、类型任意组合搜活动，结果还要能被 CDN 和缓存复用。
scenario_en: Users search events by any mix of keyword, date, and category, and the results should still be cacheable by a CDN.
q: 搜索 API 的形态是？
q_en: What should the search API look like?
options: GET /events/search 带查询参数，返回 Event[]
POST /search，请求体里直接塞一整段拼好的 SQL 查询语句
GET /events 拿到全部数据后在客户端过滤
用 WebSocket 长连接持续推送搜索结果
why: 搜索本质是带查询参数的一次性 GET 请求，参数化就能覆盖关键词、日期、类型等任意组合。
why_en: Search is just a one-shot GET request with query parameters, which is enough to cover any combination of keyword, date, or type filters.
options_en: GET /events/search with query params, returning Event[].
POST /search with a full hand-assembled SQL query statement in the request body.
GET /events fetches everything and the client filters it.
A persistent WebSocket connection keeps pushing search results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种支持客户端和服务器双向实时通信的持久连接协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a persistent connection protocol that lets client and server send messages to each other in real time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来查询和操作关系型数据库的结构化查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language used to read and write relational databases.

optionExplanations: GET /events/search 带查询参数是标准搜索端点，关键词、日期、类型等任意组合都能表达。
把 SQL 直接暴露给客户端拼装，等于让客户端能注入任意查询，安全风险极高。
全量拉取到客户端再过滤，活动量一大带宽和延迟都扛不住。
搜索是一次性请求-响应，不需要 WebSocket 这种常驻双向连接。
optionExplanations_en: GET /events/search with query params is the standard search endpoint — any combination of keyword, date, or type fits as params.
Exposing raw SQL for the client to assemble means it can inject arbitrary queries — a serious security risk.
Pulling the full dataset to filter client-side won't survive at scale — bandwidth and latency both blow up.
Search is a one-shot request/response; it doesn't need a persistent bidirectional connection like WebSocket.

scenario: 热门场次结账要花 1-2 分钟，最多的投诉是用户填完卡号才发现票已被抢走。
scenario_en: Checkout takes one to two minutes on a hot show, and the top complaint is finding the ticket gone after typing in a card number.
q: 订票 API 起步版是 POST /bookings/:eventId（body 带 ticketIds 和支付信息，返回 bookingId），后续会怎么演进？
q_en: How will the starter POST /bookings/:eventId booking API evolve?
options: 把订票请求改成 GET 以便浏览器缓存
把整个订票 API 换成 GraphQL 接口
拆成预留和确认两个端点
维持现在这版 API，不需要任何演进
why: 起步版会让用户填完支付信息才发现票没了，所以要演进成先预留、再确认的两步流程。
why_en: The starter booking API lets users fill out payment only to find the ticket is gone, so it evolves into a reserve-then-confirm two-step flow.
options_en: Change the booking request to GET so it can be cached.
Replace the whole booking API with a GraphQL interface.
Split into two endpoints: one to reserve, one to confirm.
Keep the current API as-is, no evolution needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种让客户端按需指定返回字段的 API 查询语言，是 REST 的替代风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is an API query language that lets clients specify exactly which fields they want back.

optionExplanations: 订票是有副作用的写操作，改成 GET 让浏览器缓存没有意义，还会破坏语义。
GraphQL 解决的是灵活查询问题，不能解决先预留再确认的时序问题。
拆成预留和确认两个端点，能先短暂锁住票再等支付结果，避免用户付完款才发现票没了。
维持起步版不变，用户会在填完支付信息后才发现票被抢走，体验很差。
optionExplanations_en: Booking is a write with side effects; making it GET for browser caching is meaningless and breaks semantics.
GraphQL solves flexible querying, not the timing problem of reserve-then-confirm.
Splitting into reserve and confirm endpoints holds the ticket briefly while payment completes, avoiding a post-payment surprise.
Keeping the starter version means users discover the ticket was taken only after filling out payment — a poor experience.

scenario: API 设计阶段时间有限，而且还不知道后面 deep dive 会如何改动设计。
scenario_en: API design time is limited, and later deep dives may change the contract.
q: 对起步 API 的正确态度是？
q_en: What is the right attitude toward the starter API?
options: 一次性设计出最终版完整 API 契约
先给简单 API，声明会随设计演进
跳过 API 设计，直接开始画架构图
把 Event 对象的所有字段逐一念给面试官
why: 45 分钟内契约必然会被后面的深挖推翻，先给简单端点、声明会演进最省时间。
why_en: Since later deep dives will reshape the API anyway, starting with a simple endpoint and flagging that it will evolve is the time-efficient move.
whenOtherWins: 若这轮是 API 设计专项面试，或面试官明确要字段级契约，才值得展开完整 schema。
tradeoff: 推进速度 vs API 契约完整度
options_en: Design the final, complete API contract right away.
Start with a simple API and say it will evolve as the design progresses.
Skip API design and jump straight into the architecture diagram.
Read out every field of the Event object to the interviewer.
optionExplanations: 一次性设计出最终契约几乎必被后面的 deep dive 推翻，只有已经明确不会再深挖时才划算。
先给简单端点、声明会演进，能把时间留给后面必然发生的设计调整。
跳过接口讨论会让面试官觉得准备不足并追问，除非面试官明确表示这轮不看 API。
逐字段念完整 Event 对象会挤占留给高层设计的时间，只有这轮是 API 设计专项面试时才值得。
optionExplanations_en: Designing a final contract up front almost always gets overturned by the later deep dive — only worth it with no deep dive coming.
Starting with a simple endpoint and flagging it will evolve saves time for the design changes that are coming anyway.
Skipping the interface entirely reads as under-prepared, unless the interviewer explicitly says API isn't in scope.
Reciting every field of the Event object eats into time for high-level design — only worth it in an API-focused round.

scenario: 客户端只认一个域名，后面有 Event、Search、Booking 三个服务，认证和限流也要统一做。
scenario_en: Clients talk to one domain while three services sit behind it, and auth plus rate limiting need one place to live.
q: API Gateway 在这个设计里的职责是？
q_en: What is the API Gateway's role in this design?
options: 把用户的登录会话数据长期持久化存储并管理在这一层
直接对数据库执行订票这类写事务操作
在服务端把座位图渲染成图片再返回给前端
作为入口路由请求到各微服务，并处理认证/限流/日志
why: 网关是所有客户端请求的统一入口，核心职责是路由，同时可顺带处理认证、限流这类通用逻辑。
why_en: The API Gateway is the single entry point for every client request, mainly routing traffic while optionally handling shared concerns like auth and rate limiting.
options_en: Persist and manage the user's login session data long-term at this layer.
Execute the booking write transaction directly against the database.
Render the seat map into an image on the server and hand it back.
Act as the entry point that routes requests to microservices and handles auth/rate limiting/logging.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端请求的统一入口，负责把请求路由到对应的微服务，并可处理认证、限流等横切逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API Gateway is the single entry point that routes client requests to the right microservice and can also handle cross-cutting concerns like auth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制单位时间内允许通过的请求数量，防止系统被打垮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rate limiting caps how many requests are allowed in a given time window to protect the system from overload.

termDefinitions.meaning: 认证、日志、限流这类不属于某个具体业务、但几乎每个请求都要处理的通用逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-cutting concerns are generic behaviors like auth or logging that apply across almost every request, not tied to one business feature.

optionExplanations: 会话存储和管理通常属于应用服务或专门的会话存储组件，不是网关该扛的职责。
订票事务需要业务逻辑和数据库访问，这些不该放在网关这一层做。
座位图渲染是前端职责，网关不碰 UI 层的工作。
所有客户端流量先到网关统一分发，认证、限流这类跨服务通用的事顺手在这一层解决。
optionExplanations_en: Session storage and management usually belong to the application service or a dedicated session store, not the gateway.
Booking transactions need business logic and database access — that doesn't belong at the gateway layer.
Rendering the seat map is a frontend job; the gateway doesn't touch UI work.
All client traffic lands at the gateway first for dispatch, and cross-cutting concerns like auth and rate limiting get handled there too.

scenario: 用户打开活动详情页只是读数据，这条链路上不该出现任何支付或写事务。
scenario_en: Opening an event page is a pure read, so no payment call or write transaction belongs on that path.
q: 用户访问 /event/:eventId 查看活动时，请求的正确路径是？
q_en: What is the correct request path when a user opens /event/:eventId?
options: 客户端 → API Gateway → Event Service → Events DB → 原路返回
客户端跳过网关，直接连上 Events DB 读数据
客户端 → API Gateway → Booking Service → Stripe → 完成支付
客户端 → CDN → Stripe → 数据库读取活动数据后返回
why: 查看请求走读路径：网关转发给 Event Service，服务查数据库拿 event/venue/performer 后原路返回。
why_en: A view request follows the read path: the gateway forwards to Event Service, which queries the database and returns the event, venue, and performer data.
options_en: Client -> API Gateway -> Event Service -> Events DB -> response travels back the same way.
Client skips the gateway and connects straight to Events DB to read the data.
Client -> API Gateway -> Booking Service -> Stripe -> payment completed.
Client -> CDN -> Stripe -> database fetches the event data and returns it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端请求的统一入口，负责把请求路由到对应的微服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API Gateway is the single entry point that forwards client requests to the right backend service.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第三方支付处理服务商，负责实际扣款和支付状态通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stripe is a third-party payment processor that handles charging cards and notifying the app of payment status.

optionExplanations: 标准读路径是逐层转发：网关收到请求转给对应服务，服务查库拿数据，再原样回传给客户端。
客户端直连数据库会暴露内部存储，也失去网关统一鉴权和扩展的能力。
查看活动详情不涉及订票或支付，走 Booking/Stripe 是把两条不同流程搞混了。
CDN 和 Stripe 都不参与活动详情的读取路径，这条路线对不上真实调用链。
optionExplanations_en: The standard read path forwards layer by layer: the gateway hands off to the service, the service queries the store, and the answer travels back the same way.
Letting the client connect straight to the database exposes internal storage and loses unified auth and scaling.
Viewing event details doesn't involve booking or payment — routing through Booking/Stripe conflates two different flows.
Neither CDN nor Stripe sits on the event-detail read path — this route doesn't match the actual call chain.

scenario: 开售峰值下 API Gateway 扩到 20 个实例 × 每实例数千连接，各请求耗时差异很大。
scenario_en: At peak the API gateway runs twenty instances, each holding thousands of connections, and request durations vary a lot.
q: 搜索请求流程里，负载均衡器把请求路由给哪个 API Gateway 实例？
q_en: Which API Gateway instance should the load balancer send a search request to?
options: 随机选择的实例
地理位置最近的实例
连接数最少的实例
CPU 最空闲的实例
why: 负载均衡器按 least connections 策略选实例，把新请求导向当前负载最轻的那个网关实例。
why_en: The load balancer uses least connections, sending each new request to whichever gateway instance currently has the fewest active connections.
options_en: A randomly chosen instance.
The geographically nearest instance.
The instance with the fewest active connections (least connections).
The instance with the most free CPU.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种负载均衡算法，把新请求发给当前处理连接数最少的实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least connections is a load-balancing algorithm that sends each new request to the instance currently handling the fewest active connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端请求的统一入口，负责把请求路由到对应的微服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API Gateway is the single entry point that forwards client requests to the right backend service.

optionExplanations: 随机分发长期来看各实例负载可能不均，不是原文描述的策略。
原文的搜索流程没有提到按地理位置路由这回事。
谁在处理的请求少就把新流量导给谁，这样每台实例吃到的负载会比随机分发更均匀。
负载均衡器通常不实时采集每台实例的 CPU 指标，这不是它的路由依据。
optionExplanations_en: Random distribution can leave instances unevenly loaded over time, and it's not what the article describes.
The article's search flow never mentions routing by geographic proximity.
Whichever instance is handling the fewest requests gets the next one, which keeps load more even than handing it out at random.
Load balancers typically don't collect real-time CPU metrics per instance, so that's not the routing basis here.

scenario: 订票必须保证一张票绝不能同时卖给两个用户（无双重预订）。
scenario_en: Booking must guarantee that one ticket can never be sold to two users.
q: 数据库选型的关键依据是？
q_en: What decides the database choice for booking?
options: 图数据库，建模座位邻接关系
ACID 事务数据库，配隔离级别与行锁/OCC
纯内存数据库，追求最快写入
NoSQL 数据库，靠水平分片扩展硬扛高并发
options_en: A graph database that models seat-adjacency relationships.
An ACID-transactional database with isolation levels plus row-level locking or OCC.
A pure in-memory database chasing the fastest possible writes.
A NoSQL database that scales out via sharding to absorb high concurrency.
why: 决定性约束是杜绝双订：只有 ACID 事务能保证同一时刻只有一人订到票，再靠隔离级别+行级锁或 OCC 兜住并发。
why_en: The scenario requires zero double booking, so the database must give ACID transactions plus isolation levels and row-level locking or OCC.
tradeoff: ACID 事务保证 vs 纯粹的写入速度/水平扩展能力
whenOtherWins: MySQL、DynamoDB 等只要支持事务同样可行——决定性属性是 ACID 本身，不是 PostgreSQL 这个具体引擎。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组保证事务安全的性质：原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID describes four transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 乐观并发控制：先允许并发操作，提交前才检查冲突，冲突就重试或失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control lets operations proceed concurrently and only checks for conflicts at commit time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁住被修改的那一行，不影响表里其他行的并发访问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row-level lock blocks other transactions from changing only that specific row until it's released.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库控制并发事务之间可见性和冲突处理程度的设置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Isolation level controls how much concurrent transactions can see or interfere with each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以节点和边为核心存储结构、擅长表达复杂关系的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A graph database stores data as nodes and edges and excels at modeling complex relationships.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常为扩展性牺牲部分事务/关系能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is a broad label for non-relational databases that often trade transactional strength for scalability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据主要保存在内存而非磁盘、以读写速度为卖点的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-memory database keeps data primarily in RAM rather than on disk to maximize speed.

optionExplanations: 图数据库擅长表达实体关系，但座位邻接关系不是本题瓶颈，双订才是——只有真要建模复杂关系图时才该选它。
ACID 事务把检查和改状态打包成不可分割的操作，配隔离级别与行锁/OCC，保证同一时刻只有一人订到票。
纯内存数据库写入快，但掉电易丢单，且多数缺原生事务防双订，只在能接受这个风险时才划算。
多数 NoSQL 弱化事务换取水平扩展，双订风险反而更高，只有能容忍最终一致时才适合。
optionExplanations_en: Graph databases excel at relationships, but seat adjacency isn't the bottleneck — double-booking is; only worth it if you truly need a relationship graph.
ACID transactions bundle check-and-update into one atomic operation with isolation levels and row locks/OCC, guaranteeing only one person books a seat.
A pure in-memory store writes fast but risks losing orders on power loss and often lacks native transactions — only worth that risk if acceptable.
Most NoSQL stores trade away transactions for horizontal scale, which raises double-booking risk — only fits when eventual consistency is tolerable.

scenario: 订票要在一个事务里同时改 tickets 和写 bookings，两张表强耦合。
scenario_en: Booking has to update tickets and insert into bookings inside one transaction, so the two tables are tightly coupled.
q: 多个服务共用同一个数据库违反了「database per service」教条，为什么这题里共库反而是对的？
q_en: Why is a shared database acceptable here despite the database-per-service rule?
options: 误以为 Postgres 单实例装不下多个数据库
认为共库单纯是为了省服务器成本
数据强耦合+需要跨表事务，拆库反而只添复杂度
其实是错的，面试里必须严格拆库
options_en: The misconception that a single Postgres instance can't hold multiple databases.
Treating shared-database as purely a cost-saving move.
The tables are tightly coupled and booking needs a cross-table transaction, so splitting only adds complexity.
It's actually wrong — interviews require strict database-per-service.
why: bookings/tickets/events 强耦合且订票要跨表事务，共库更直接；面试要按场景权衡，而非死守这条微服务教条。
why_en: The tables are tightly coupled and booking needs a cross-table transaction, so sharing one database is the direct call, not blindly following the database-per-service rule.

termDefinitions.meaning: 微服务架构惯例：每个服务拥有独立数据库，别的服务不能直接访问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Database-per-service is a microservices convention where each service owns its own database and others can't access it directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个操作打包成原子单元，要么全部生效要么全部不生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ACID transaction bundles multiple operations so they either all succeed or all fail together.

optionExplanations: 一个数据库实例本就能建多个逻辑库，这不是共库的真正理由。
省钱只是次要收益，真正原因是数据耦合和事务需求，不是成本考量。
三张表互相牵着走、订票还得跨表原子更新，硬拆成三个库只会把这层耦合变成分布式事务的麻烦。
「一服务一库」是默认建议不是铁律，面试要按场景权衡，教条化拆库才是真正的错误。
optionExplanations_en: A single database instance can already host multiple logical databases — that's not the real reason for sharing one here.
Cost savings is a side benefit at best; the real driver is data coupling and transaction needs, not budget.
The three tables are pulled together by a cross-table atomic update on booking, so splitting them just turns that coupling into a distributed-transaction headache.
"One service, one database" is a default guideline, not a hard rule; dogmatically splitting it here would be the actual mistake.

scenario: 简单版订票：用户已提交支付信息，系统必须保证同一张票不会被卖两次。
scenario_en: In the simple booking flow the user has already submitted payment details, and the system must guarantee no seat is sold twice.
q: 简单版订票流程里，Booking Service 发起的事务包含哪三步？
q_en: What three steps happen inside the Booking Service transaction?
options: 检查票是否可用 → 状态改为 booked → 写入 Bookings 订单记录
校验支付方式是否有效 → 生成一封收据邮件 → 更新场馆库存表数据
先创建一条订单记录 → 再通知场馆管理员到场处理 → 最后打印一张纸质票据留底
锁定整张票表不放 → 逐行更新每一个座位状态 → 才释放整张表的锁
options_en: Check ticket availability -> flip its status to booked -> write a new record into the Bookings table.
Validate the payment method -> generate a receipt email -> update the venue inventory table.
First create an order record -> then notify the venue manager to attend -> finally print a paper ticket to keep on file.
Lock the entire ticket table first -> update every seat's status row by row -> only then release the table lock.
why: 一个事务里做三件事：查可用性、把票改为 booked、插入订单记录；若因别人先订而失败，就给客户端返回失败。
why_en: The transaction checks availability, flips the ticket to booked, and inserts a booking record, all in one atomic step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个数据库操作打包成一个不可分割的整体，要么全部生效要么全部回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction bundles several database operations into one atomic unit that either all commit or all roll back.

optionExplanations: 三步都在同一个事务里：查可用性、改为 booked、插入订单记录，任一步失败整体回滚。
支付校验其实由 Stripe 单独处理，收据/场馆库存也不在这个数据库事务里。
通知管理员、打印票据是线下流程，发生在事务外，不是防双订的机制。
锁整张表会让所有并发订票请求排队等待，是性能灾难，不是三步事务的做法。
optionExplanations_en: All three steps run in one transaction: check availability, flip to booked, insert the order row — a failure rolls back everything.
Payment validation is actually handled separately by Stripe; receipts and venue inventory aren't part of this transaction either.
Notifying admins and printing tickets are offline steps outside the transaction, not part of the anti-double-booking mechanism.
Locking the entire table would queue every concurrent booking request — a performance disaster, not the three-step transaction.

scenario: 热门场次同一张票有上百人同时点，而结账流程要 1-2 分钟才走完。
scenario_en: Hundreds of people click the same seat on a hot show, and checkout still takes one to two minutes to finish.
q: 简单版订票设计（无预留机制）的根本缺陷是？
q_en: What is the fundamental flaw in the simple booking flow without reservations?
options: 事务保护失效，导致数据库双重预订
系统架构上无法支持一次买多张票
Booking Service 没法对接 Stripe 收款
用户填完支付表单才发现票被抢走，体验很差
options_en: Transaction protection fails, so the database ends up double-booking tickets.
The architecture can't support buying multiple tickets in one order.
The Booking Service can't integrate with Stripe for payment.
Users fill out the payment form only to find the ticket was already grabbed by someone faster.
why: 没有预留，票在结账过程中随时可能被抢；事务保证不会双订，但用户白填支付信息，体验很差。
why_en: Without a reservation step, the ticket can be grabbed by someone else while the user is still filling out payment details, wasting their time even though the transaction still prevents true double booking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第三方支付处理平台，负责实际扣款和状态回调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stripe is a third-party payment processor that charges the card and reports the result back.

optionExplanations: 事务本身没坏，它仍能挡住真正的双重预订，问题不在一致性。
Booking 表的 ticketIds 本就是列表，一次买多张票在架构上没有限制。
Stripe 对接是独立模块，跟有没有预留机制无关。
结账窗口内票随时可能被抢，用户白白填完支付信息才发现票没了，体验很差。
optionExplanations_en: The transaction itself isn't broken — it still stops a real double-booking, so this isn't a consistency problem.
The Booking table's ticketIds is already a list, so buying multiple tickets isn't architecturally limited.
Stripe integration is a separate module, unrelated to whether a reservation mechanism exists.
During the checkout window the ticket can be grabbed by someone else, so the user fills out payment only to find it's gone.

scenario: 团队不想自己接触信用卡号，也不想承担 PCI 合规，但要在付款成功后立刻改票状态。
scenario_en: The team doesn't want to touch card numbers or take on PCI compliance, yet ticket state must flip right after payment succeeds.
q: Stripe 在这个架构中的角色是？
q_en: What role does Stripe play in this architecture?
options: 内部数据库，负责持久化票据状态
外部支付服务，处理交易并在确认后回调通知
反向代理式负载均衡器，负责跨节点流量分发
内存缓存层，负责加速热点数据读取
options_en: An internal database that persists ticket state.
An external payment service that processes the charge and calls back once confirmed.
A reverse-proxy load balancer that distributes traffic across nodes.
An in-memory cache layer that speeds up hot reads.
why: 支付交给外部 Stripe 处理，完成后通过 webhook 通知 Booking Service，服务再把票改为 sold、订单改为 confirmed。
why_en: Stripe is the external payment processor, and once it confirms the charge it notifies the Booking Service via webhook so the ticket can be marked sold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第三方支付处理平台，负责实际扣款和状态回调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stripe is a third-party payment processor that charges the card and reports the result back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种事件通知机制：第三方在事情发生后主动向你的服务器发 HTTP 请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A webhook is an HTTP callback a third-party service sends to your server when an event happens.

optionExplanations: 票据状态实际存在 Events DB 里，Stripe 不负责持久化票据数据。
支付这一步交给外部的 Stripe 去跑，跑完它主动回调通知，服务这边再把票和订单标为终态。
Stripe 完全不参与跨节点流量路由，跟负载均衡器是两回事。
Stripe 不缓存也不加速任何读请求，它只处理支付交易。
optionExplanations_en: Ticket state is actually stored in the Events DB — Stripe doesn't persist ticket data.
The charge itself runs on Stripe outside this system, and once it finishes Stripe calls back so the service can mark the ticket and order final.
Stripe plays no part in cross-node traffic routing — that's a completely different job from a load balancer.
Stripe doesn't cache or accelerate any read request; it only processes payment transactions.

scenario: 面试还在高层设计阶段，搜索先要有一个能跑通的版本，性能问题留到 deep dive 再解。
scenario_en: You're still in high-level design, so search just needs a version that works; performance gets fixed later in the deep dive.
q: 起步版搜索（Search Service 直接按 API 参数过滤查询 SQL 库）的定位是？
q_en: How should you frame the starter SQL-based search implementation?
options: 功能可用但有性能隐患，是后续 deep dive 优化的起点
已经是可以直接上线的最终定稿方案，完全不需要再做任何优化了
整个设计从根上就完全不可行，面试中根本不该被提出来
只适合写多读少、查询量非常小的边缘系统场景
options_en: It works functionally but carries performance risk, and it's the starting point later deep dives optimize.
It's already the final, production-ready design and needs no further optimization at all.
The whole design is fundamentally unworkable and shouldn't even be proposed in an interview.
It only fits write-heavy systems with a very small query volume.
why: 直接查库过滤是合理起点：功能对但关键词模糊匹配会全表扫描、扛不住规模；面试里先给能用的简单方案，再在 deep dive 里演进。
why_en: A direct filtered query is a reasonable starting point that works but will full-scan on wildcard keyword matches, so it's meant to be improved in later deep dives, not the final answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 查询没有可用索引命中，只能逐行扫描整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full table scan means the query has no usable index and must check every row.

optionExplanations: 直接查库过滤功能上能跑，但关键词模糊匹配会全表扫描，是后续 deep dive 优化的合理起点。
把第一版当终稿会漏掉后面全文索引/Elasticsearch 这类必要优化。
把「不是最优」误判成「不可行」——作为面试起点完全合理，只是不是终点。
订票系统读远多于写（100:1），这个方案恰恰在读多时最吃力，适用边界说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Filtering directly against the database works, but keyword matching triggers a full scan — a reasonable starting point for later optimization.
Treating the first version as final would skip the full-text-index/Elasticsearch upgrade actually needed later.
Confusing "not optimal" with "not viable" — it's a completely reasonable interview starting point, just not the ending point.
Reads far outnumber writes here (100:1), and this approach struggles exactly when reads dominate — the applicability is backwards.

scenario: 用户选座后有 10 分钟结账倒计时，弃单率很高，票不能被无限占着。
scenario_en: A user gets a ten-minute checkout countdown, abandonment is common, and seats cannot stay held forever.
q: 预留票（带倒计时的锁票机制）需要同时满足哪三个要求？
q_en: What three requirements must the ticket reservation mechanism satisfy?
options: 要给每张票加密、要审计每一次锁定操作、要定期全量备份数据
要限流控制访问、要排队等待、要缓存座位图数据
结账锁给该用户；弃单释放他人；完成置为 sold 确认订单
要锁票、要扣款成功、要发确认短信给用户
options_en: Encrypt every ticket, audit every single lock action, and back up all data on a schedule.
Rate-limit access, make people queue, and cache the seat map data.
Lock it for the buyer at checkout, release it on abandonment, mark it sold and confirm the order on completion.
Lock the ticket, get the charge to succeed, and text the user a confirmation.
why: 预留机制的三要素：结账时独占、超时/放弃自动释放、完成后落定为已售；后面的候选方案都围绕这三点评估。
why_en: A reservation lock must exclusively hold the seat during checkout, auto-release it on timeout or abandonment, and finalize it as sold once payment completes.

rows: 票在结账窗口内只锁给这一人
放弃或超时后库存自动还给他人
支付成功后票改 sold 并确认订单

optionExplanations: 加密、审计、全量备份都合理，但它们都不解决「票会被别人抢走」这个核心问题。
限流、排队、缓存是应对高并发访问量的手段，不是锁票规则本身的要求。
三要素分别对应：结账时独占该票、弃单或超时自动释放给别人、完成购买后落定为已售。
扣款成功、发确认短信属于支付后的动作，不是预留锁机制的定义。
optionExplanations_en: Encryption, auditing, and full backups are all reasonable, but none solves the core problem of the seat being grabbed by someone else.
Rate limiting, queuing, and caching handle high traffic volume — they're not requirements of the lock mechanism itself.
The three requirements: hold the seat exclusively during checkout, auto-release on abandonment/timeout, lock in as sold on completion.
Successful charge and confirmation SMS are post-payment actions, not part of what defines the reservation lock.

scenario: 要在用户结账的十来分钟里锁住这张票。有人提议：开一个数据库事务，用 SELECT FOR UPDATE 锁行，等用户付完款再提交。
scenario_en: A proposal keeps a database transaction open with SELECT FOR UPDATE while the user spends about ten minutes checking out.
q: 对这个「长时间交互式事务」方案的正确评价是？
q_en: How should you judge the long interactive transaction proposal?
options: 好方案，数据库原生支持行锁
坏方案：长期占锁耗资源、加剧竞争死锁，还可能锁悬置
加 lock_timeout 设个超时上限就没问题
比 Redis 更好，因为强一致
options_en: Good idea — the database natively supports row locks.
Bad idea: holding the lock that long strains resources, worsens contention and deadlocks, and can leave locks stuck.
Just add a lock_timeout as an upper time bound and it's fine.
Better than Redis because it's strongly consistent.
why: 长时间持行锁会拖垮数据库、放大竞争与死锁；lock_timeout 只让用户看到报错而非被排队，放弃结账时锁还可能悬置。
why_en: Holding a row lock for the whole checkout window strains the database and risks contention or deadlocks, and lock_timeout just trades a stuck lock for a user-facing error instead of solving it.
tradeoff: 短临界区行锁 vs 横跨整个结账流程的长事务锁
whenOtherWins: SELECT FOR UPDATE 适合真正短的临界区，比如最终确认落库那一瞬间，而不是整个结账过程。

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 语句，在事务内锁住查到的行，阻止其他事务并发修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE is a PostgreSQL statement that locks the selected rows inside a transaction so no other transaction can modify them concurrently.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨越用户操作等待时间、持续打开很久才提交的数据库事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interactive (long-running) transaction stays open across user think-time instead of committing almost instantly.

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 配置项，等待锁超过这个时间就让事务失败退出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: lock_timeout is a PostgreSQL setting that fails a transaction if it waits too long to acquire a lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个及以上事务互相等待对方持有的锁，导致谁都无法继续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock happens when two or more transactions wait on locks held by each other and none can proceed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁住被修改的那一行，不影响表里其他行的并发访问。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row-level lock blocks modification of just that row while leaving other rows free for concurrent access.

optionExplanations: 行锁本身没错，错在把它跨十分钟的整个结账流程长期持有——原生支持不代表这么用是对的。
十分钟级别持锁远超近乎瞬时的设计初衷，耗资源、加剧竞争死锁，弃单时锁还可能悬置。
lock_timeout 只是个超时上限，把「锁悬置」换成「用户看到报错」，体验依然差，还得额外处理应用层重试。
Postgres 的一致性保证和这个锁方案会不会阻塞其他人是两回事，强一致不能替它洗白。
optionExplanations_en: Row locks aren't the problem — native support doesn't make holding one across a ten-minute checkout the right way to use it.
Holding a lock for ten minutes far exceeds the near-instant intent — it burns resources, worsens deadlocks, and can leave locks stuck.
A lock_timeout is just an upper bound — it trades a stuck lock for a user-facing error, still bad, and pushes retry handling to the app layer.
Postgres's consistency guarantee is separate from whether this locking blocks everyone else — strong consistency doesn't excuse it.

scenario: 预留机制先用最简单的做法实现，此时还不打算引入 Redis 这类额外组件。
scenario_en: You want the simplest possible reservation mechanism first, without pulling in an extra component like Redis yet.
q: Good 方案：在 Ticket 表上加什么来实现预留？
q_en: What should the Good reservation design add to the Ticket table?
options: status 字段(三态)+过期时间戳，cron 定期重置超时票
只加一个布尔型 locked 标记列，靠应用层单独记录预留时间
写数据库触发器，在过期后自动删除这张预留票
把预留中的票整体复制进一张独立临时表管理
options_en: Add a three-state status field plus an expiration timestamp, with a cron job resetting timed-out rows.
Just add a single boolean locked column and separately track the reservation time at the app layer.
Write a database trigger that auto-deletes the ticket once it expires.
Copy reserved tickets wholesale into a separate temp table to manage them.
why: 选票时状态从 available 改为 reserved 并记时间戳；完成购买改为 booked；放弃则由 cron 扫描超时的 reserved 行重置回 available。
why_en: The ticket gets a three-state status plus an expiration timestamp, and a cron job periodically resets timed-out reservations back to available.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间表周期性执行任务的调度机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cron is a scheduler that runs a job repeatedly on a fixed interval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录实体当前所处阶段的字段，这里是 available/reserved/booked 三态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A status field records which stage an entity is currently in — here available, reserved, or booked.

optionExplanations: 三态状态机能区分「预留中」和「已售出」，配过期时间戳和 cron 定期重置，这是原文的 Good 方案。
布尔值只能表达锁定/未锁定两态，装不下 available、reserved、sold 三种不同状态。
触发器删除票会把票本身删掉，而不是把它释放回可预订，票据反而丢了。
复制到临时表要保持两张表同步，预留和释放都要写两遍，增加一致性负担。
optionExplanations_en: The three-state machine distinguishes reserved from sold, paired with an expiry timestamp and a cron sweep — the article's Good approach.
A boolean only expresses locked/unlocked, not the three distinct states of available, reserved, and sold.
A trigger that deletes on expiry removes the ticket row entirely instead of releasing it — the ticket itself is gone.
Copying into a temp table means keeping two tables in sync — both reserve and release get written twice, adding overhead.

scenario: 热门场次每分钟上千次弃单，而 cron 每 5 分钟才扫一次过期预留。
scenario_en: A hot show sees thousands of abandoned carts a minute while the cron job only sweeps expired holds every five minutes.
q: cron 定时释放过期预留的两大缺陷是？
q_en: What are the two main flaws of releasing expired reservations with cron?
options: 写放大会变得很严重，磁盘 I/O 成本会跟着一起飙升
跟 Postgres 底层的事务隔离机制根本水火不容
cron 清理任务一旦跑慢或积压，就会直接导致同一张票被双重预订
解锁有延迟，热门票过期后仍占位；cron 故障会让预留长期卡死
options_en: Write amplification gets severe and disk I/O cost climbs right along with it.
It's fundamentally at odds with Postgres's underlying transaction isolation.
A slow or backed-up cron cleanup job directly causes the same ticket to get double-booked.
There's an unlock delay leaving hot tickets stuck past their hold, and a failed cron job leaves reservations stuck indefinitely.
why: cron 有固有滞后：票已过期却还占着不可买，热门活动尤其伤；cron 本身故障会让预留迟迟不释放，造成客诉和收入损失。
why_en: Cron-based release has an inherent delay that leaves expired tickets locked until the next run, which hurts hot events, and if the cron job itself fails, reservations can stay stuck indefinitely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间表周期性执行任务的调度机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cron is a scheduler that runs a job repeatedly on a fixed interval.

optionExplanations: cron 批量更新的写量其实有限，写放大不是这里的主要痛点。
cron 只是普通的周期任务，跟数据库事务机制没有冲突。
双重预订仍由事务和行锁挡住，cron 跑慢或积压顶多让票暂时不可买，突破不了这层防线。
cron 存在固有滞后，热门票过期后仍占位，一旦 cron 本身故障，预留会长期卡死无法释放。
optionExplanations_en: Cron's batch updates are limited in volume — write amplification isn't the real pain point here.
Cron is just a periodic job with no conflict with the database's transaction mechanism.
Double-booking is still blocked by the transaction and row locks — a slow or backed-up cron only delays availability, not a real breach.
Cron has inherent lag, so a hot ticket sits locked after expiring, and if cron itself fails, reservations get stuck indefinitely.

scenario: 开售峰值下 cron 的分钟级滞后不可接受：票一过期就必须马上能被别人抢到。
scenario_en: At on-sale a minutes-long cron lag is unacceptable — the instant a hold expires someone else must be able to grab the seat.
q: Better 方案（无 cron 依赖）的核心洞察是什么？
q_en: What is the core insight in the Better no-cron reservation design?
options: 把预留锁的整套状态都挪进应用进程的内存变量里去管理
可预留=AVAILABLE或过期RESERVED，短事务内原子改写
把每一次预留请求都依次丢进消息队列里排队串行处理
把票的过期时间字段单独拆出去，另外存到一张新的预留状态表里统一管理
options_en: Move the entire reservation-lock state into an application-process memory variable to manage it.
A ticket is reservable when it's AVAILABLE or a stale RESERVED past its hold, checked and flipped atomically inside one short transaction.
Push every single reservation request into a message queue and process them one by one in order.
Split the hold-expiry timestamp out and store it in a new dedicated reservation-status table to manage centrally.
why: 票的真实状态是两个属性的组合：available，或 reserved 但已过期；短事务内先判断这个组合再改为 reserved，完全不依赖 cron 的及时性。
why_en: A ticket is reservable when it's either available or a reserved-but-expired row, and checking plus flipping that state happens inside one short transaction with no dependency on cron timing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只做一次快速读判断加写入、几乎瞬时提交的数据库事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A short transaction does one quick check-and-write and commits almost instantly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次操作要么整体生效要么整体不生效，不会停在中间状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Atomicity means an operation either fully applies or not at all, never leaving a half-done state.

optionExplanations: 应用内存状态在多实例部署下不共享，挡不住跨实例的双重预订。
一张票能不能预留，取决于它现在是空的、还是一个已经超时的旧预留，这个判断和改写全在一次短事务里原子完成。
队列能串行处理请求，但解决不了同一时刻多用户抢同一票的原子性判断，还多了额外延迟。
拆到另一张预留状态表只是搬了数据位置，判断和更新依然要跨表协调，原子性问题没解决。
optionExplanations_en: In-memory application state isn't shared across instances, so it can't stop double-booking across instances.
Whether a seat can be reserved comes down to one atomic check inside a single short transaction: is it open, or is it a stale reservation that's timed out.
A queue serializes requests but doesn't solve the atomic decision of who wins when multiple users grab the same seat, and it adds latency.
Splitting expiry into a separate reservation-status table just relocates the data — the check and update still need cross-table coordination.

q: 补全 Better 方案的事务伪代码：
q_en: Fill in the Better design's transaction pseudocode.
text: 开启{{事务}} → 检查票是 AVAILABLE 或 RESERVED 但已{{过期}} → 更新为 RESERVED 并把过期时间设为 now + {{10}} 分钟 → 提交。
why: 整个判断和更新压缩进一个短事务，数据库原子性保证并发下只有一人能改成功，过期预留也能被直接接管，不必等 cron。
why_en: The check and the update happen inside one short transaction, so atomicity ensures only one user can win under concurrency, and expired reservations can be reclaimed immediately without waiting on cron.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个数据库操作打包成一个不可分割的整体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction bundles multiple database operations into one atomic unit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 票的初始状态：尚未被任何人预留或购买。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AVAILABLE means the ticket hasn't been reserved or bought by anyone yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 票已被某用户锁定，等待其完成支付或超时释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RESERVED means a user is holding the ticket while checking out, pending payment or expiry.

scenario: Better 方案要上线，先说清它给读路径和日常运维新增了什么成本。
scenario_en: Before shipping the Better design you need to say what it costs on the read path and in day-to-day operations.
q: Better 方案（状态组合判断）的代价是什么，怎么缓解？
q_en: What cost does the Better state-combination design add, and how can you reduce it?
options: 会双重预订；只能靠分布式事务兜底
cron 一旦挂掉系统就瘫痪；靠加监控解决
读路径变慢；表不直观——物化视图+清扫任务缓解
无法再设置任何过期时间；只能手工处理
options_en: It causes double booking; the only fix is distributed transactions.
The whole system halts if cron goes down; fixed by more monitoring.
Reads get slower and the table is less legible — mitigated with materialized views/indexes and a sweep job.
You can no longer set any expiration time; it must be handled manually.
why: 读要多过滤一个条件而略慢，可用物化视图+复合索引缓解；表上躺着过期的 reserved 行不够直观，加清扫任务改善，且清扫延迟不影响正确性。
why_en: Reads get a bit slower from filtering two conditions, offset with materialized views and a compound index, and a sweep job can tidy up expired-looking rows without affecting correctness even if it lags.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先算好并存储的查询结果视图，读取时不用重新聚合原始表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A materialized view stores a precomputed query result so reads don't have to re-aggregate raw tables each time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时基于多个列建立的索引，加速按这几列组合过滤的查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A compound index is built on multiple columns together to speed up queries that filter on that combination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 定期把状态过期但还没被回收的行清理干净的周期性任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sweep job is a periodic task that cleans up rows whose state has expired but hasn't been reclaimed yet.

optionExplanations: 双订仍被同一原子事务挡住，这个方案本就不会双订，代价不在这里。
Better 方案压根不依赖 cron，也就没有 cron 故障这个失败模式。
读路径要多判断一个过期条件会略慢，表上还躺着已过期但没清扫的 reserved 行，可用物化视图和清扫任务缓解。
过期时间戳字段依然存在，只是从 cron 扫描改成短事务判断，不是消失了。
optionExplanations_en: Double-booking is still blocked by the same atomic transaction — this approach doesn't double-book, so that's not the actual cost.
The Better approach doesn't depend on cron at all, so a cron outage isn't a failure mode here.
The read path checks one extra expiry condition and runs a bit slower, and expired-unswept rows linger — materialized views and a sweep task help.
The expiry timestamp field still exists; it's just checked in a short transaction instead of scanned by cron.

scenario: 对比两版预留方案：当清理任务被拖慢甚至挂掉时，哪一版仍然能正确放票。
scenario_en: Compare the two reservation designs on one axis: when the cleanup job lags or dies, which one still releases seats correctly.
q: 在「清理任务延迟的影响」这个维度上，Good（cron 释放）与 Better（读时判断过期）的关键区别是？
q_en: For cleanup delay, how do Good cron release and Better read-time expiry differ?
options: Good 因 cron 跑得慢而卡票；Better 只牺牲一点可读性
两者都会因为清理任务延迟而同样造成丢票或超卖
Better 方案里清理任务一旦延迟或积压，就会直接导致双重预订超卖
Good 方案完全不需要任何周期性的清理任务存在
options_en: Good gets stuck when cron runs slow; Better only costs a bit of readability.
Both would equally lose tickets or oversell when the cleanup job is delayed.
In Better, a delayed or backed-up cleanup job would directly cause a double booking and oversell.
Good doesn't need any periodic cleanup job to exist at all.
why: Better 把过期判断内联进预留事务，清扫任务再慢也不影响正确性；Good 却依赖 cron 按时跑，cron 一慢，过期票就暂时抢不到。
why_en: Better checks expiry inside the reservation transaction itself, so a slow cleanup job never breaks correctness, while Good depends on cron running on time, and any cron delay leaves expired tickets stuck.
tradeoff: 过期判断内联进事务 vs 依赖定时任务及时执行

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间表周期性执行任务的调度机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cron is a scheduler that runs a job repeatedly on a fixed interval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只做一次快速读判断加写入、几乎瞬时提交的数据库事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A short transaction does one quick check-and-write and commits almost instantly.

optionExplanations: Good 把正确性押在 cron 及时性上，一慢过期票就暂时抢不到；Better 把过期判断做进事务本身，清扫再慢也只伤可读性。
实际上只有 Good 会因清理延迟丢失订票机会，Better 的原子判断不受清扫速度影响。
Better 的双订防护来自事务内的原子判断，跟清扫任务快慢或积压无关，清理延迟不会导致双订。
Good 恰恰依赖 cron 才能把过期票放出来，没有清理任务它永远不会释放。
optionExplanations_en: Good bets correctness on cron timing — lag leaves expired tickets stuck; Better inlines the expiry check, so a slow sweep only hurts readability.
In reality only Good loses booking opportunities to cleanup lag — Better's atomic check isn't affected by sweep speed.
Better's double-booking protection comes from the in-transaction atomic check, independent of sweep speed or backlog.
Good specifically depends on cron to release expired tickets; without a cleanup job it would never release them.

scenario: 订票系统已用 PostgreSQL 做强一致的订单事务；现在要给「选中座位后临时锁定该票」加一个到点自动释放的预留机制，团队讨论要不要再引入 Redis。
scenario_en: PostgreSQL already protects final booking transactions, but temporary seat holds need automatic expiry.
q: 引入 Redis 做预留锁的决定性理由是什么？
q_en: What is the decisive reason to introduce Redis for reservation locks?
options: Redis 把数据落盘持久化，一致性和持久性反而都比 PostgreSQL 更强
Redis 原生支持复杂的多表关联式 SQL join 查询
需要能自动过期的临时预留：PG 无原生行级 TTL，Redis 自带过期且锁更快
自建维护一整套 Redis 服务器群集几乎是零运维成本
options_en: Redis persists data to disk, giving it both stronger consistency and durability than PostgreSQL.
Redis natively supports complex multi-table relational SQL join queries.
We need a temporary hold that lapses on its own: Postgres has no native row-level TTL, and Redis gives built-in auto-lapsing keys plus faster locking.
Running a whole self-hosted Redis server cluster is basically zero ops cost.
why: 决定性约束是自动过期：Redis 自带 TTL 到点释放 key，PG 没有原生行级 TTL；内存操作也让高并发抢锁/放锁更快。
why_en: The deciding factor is automatic expiry: Redis has built-in TTL to release the hold, which Postgres lacks natively, and its in-memory ops stay fast under heavy concurrency.
tradeoff: 自动过期+锁速度 vs 多引入一个组件的运维复杂度
whenOtherWins: 若没有「临时预留自动过期」的需求（比如即点即买、无结账等待期），数据库事务加 OCC 就够，不必引入 Redis。

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，常用作缓存或分布式锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used for caching or distributed locks.

termDefinitions.meaning: key 的存活时间，到期后自动被删除或释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the time-to-live after which a key automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多台机器协调、保证同一资源同一时间只被一个客户端持有的锁机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock coordinates across machines so only one client holds a given resource at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持事务和强一致性的关系型数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PostgreSQL is a relational database with strong transactional consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库里把多张表按关联字段合并查询的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SQL join combines rows from multiple tables based on a related column.

optionExplanations: 预留数据本就该及时消失，不需要强持久化或强一致，落盘反而不是这里要的属性。
Redis 不是关系型查询引擎，没有 join 能力，这不是引入它的理由。
PG 没有原生行级 TTL，Redis 自带过期能到点自动释放锁，内存操作也让高并发抢锁更快，这是决定性约束。
自建维护一整套 Redis 服务器仍要监控告警，运维成本不为零，只是比某些方案轻。
optionExplanations_en: Reservation data is meant to lapse promptly — it needs neither strong durability nor consistency, so that's not the property sought here.
Redis isn't a relational query engine and has no join capability, so that's not the reason to bring it in.
Postgres has no native row-level TTL, while Redis auto-expires keys and its in-memory ops make lock acquisition faster — the deciding constraint.
Running your own Redis fleet still needs monitoring and alerting — the ops cost isn't zero, just lighter than some alternatives.

scenario: 预留状态搬进 Redis，确认购买时必须能核对「来确认的人就是当初预留的人」。
scenario_en: Reservation state now lives in Redis, and at confirm time you must verify the person confirming is the one who reserved.
q: 在 Redis 预留锁的设计里，key 和 value 应该分别是什么？
q_en: In the Redis reservation-lock design, what should the key and value be?
options: key=userId，value=该用户当前锁定的那一整份票列表数组
key=ticketId，value=userId：可校验确认人=预留人
key=eventId，value=当前被锁定的那个座位号
key=bookingId，value=这笔订单对应的金额
options_en: key = userId, value = that whole array of tickets the user currently has locked.
key = ticketId, value = userId: lets you verify the confirmer matches the original holder.
key = eventId, value = whichever seat number is currently locked.
key = bookingId, value = the dollar amount tied to that order.
why: 以票 ID 为 key、用户 ID 为 value 并带 TTL：一张票只有一把锁，且确认购买时能核对「确认的人就是当初预留的人」。
why_en: The key is the ticket ID and the value is the user ID with a TTL, so each ticket has exactly one lock and you can verify the confirmer is the original holder.

rows: SET key value NX EX ttl

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store.

termDefinitions.meaning: key 的存活时间，到期自动释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the time after which a key automatically expires.

optionExplanations: 以用户为 key 聚合他的票，一个用户可能同时锁多张票，一个 key 装不下唯一锁语义。
以票 ID 为 key、持有者 ID 为 value：一张票天然只有一把锁，确认购买时还能核对「确认的人=预留的人」。
以活动为 key 会让整场活动共用一把锁，粒度太粗，谁都抢不到别的座位。
金额不是锁的判断依据，也没法用来校验谁是持有者。
optionExplanations_en: Using userId as the key aggregates one user's tickets, but they might reserve several — one key can't express per-ticket lock semantics.
ticketId as key and userId as value gives each ticket exactly one lock, and lets confirmation check the confirming user matches the reserver.
Using eventId as key makes the entire event share one lock — far too coarse; nobody could grab any other seat.
The amount isn't what the lock needs to decide on, and it can't verify who holds the lock.

scenario: 要给 ticket:abc123 上一把 10 分钟的预留锁，操作必须原子，保证两个并发用户里只有一个能抢到。
scenario_en: Set a 10-minute hold on ticket:abc123 atomically, so only one of two concurrent users can get it.
q: 哪条命令是正确写法？
q_en: Which Redis command is the correct form?
options: 先 GET ticket:abc123 再 SET ticket:abc123 user456
SET ticket:abc123 user456 XX EX 600
SET ticket:abc123 user456 NX EX 600
DEL ticket:abc123 然后 SET ticket:abc123 user456
options_en: First GET ticket:abc123, then SET ticket:abc123 user456.
SET ticket:abc123 user456 XX EX 600.
SET ticket:abc123 user456 NX EX 600.
DEL ticket:abc123, then SET ticket:abc123 user456.
why: NX EX 是单条原子命令：NX 保证只有一个客户端能设置成功，EX 600 让锁 10 分钟后自动过期。
why_en: SET with NX EX is a single atomic command — NX guarantees only one client's write succeeds, and EX 600 makes the lock expire after ten minutes.
tradeoff: 原子的 SET NX EX vs 非原子的 GET+SET / DEL+SET
whenOtherWins: 一次订多张票时单条 SET 不够：要逐票顺序抢锁，失败就回滚；若票哈希到同一节点，可用 Lua 脚本让抢锁原子化。
codeSample:
# NX: key 不存在才设置（原子抢锁，并发下只有一个成功）
# EX 600: 600 秒 = 10 分钟自动过期
SET ticket:abc123 user:456 NX EX 600

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子加锁命令：NX 表示仅当 key 不存在才设置，EX 表示设置秒级过期时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SET with NX EX is Redis's atomic locking command — NX sets only if the key is absent, EX attaches a expiry in seconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要么完整执行、要么完全不执行，中途不会被其他请求打断的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic operation either completes fully or not at all, with no other request able to interleave.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个客户端同时读写同一份数据、结果取决于执行时序的错误场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition is a bug where the outcome depends on the timing of concurrent operations on shared data.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 支持在服务端原子执行的脚本，可以把多个命令合并成一次原子操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Lua script runs atomically inside Redis, letting you combine multiple commands into one atomic operation.

optionExplanations: GET 和 SET 是两条命令，中间有窗口——两个客户端可能都 GET 到「不存在」，然后都去 SET，锁被抢两次。
XX 的语义是「仅当 key 已存在才设置」，正好反了——已被锁的票才会设置成功，没人能抢到空票。
一条命令同时干两件事：抢占和设定存活时间都在这一次调用里完成，中间没有空隙让别人插队。
DEL 和 SET 之间仍有窗口，另一个客户端可能在这个间隙插队抢到锁。
optionExplanations_en: GET and SET are two separate commands with a gap between them — two clients could both GET "not found" and both SET, grabbing the lock twice.
XX means "only set if the key already exists," which is backwards — only an already-locked ticket would succeed, so no one could grab a free one.
One call does both jobs at once — claiming the key and setting its lifetime — leaving no gap for a second client to sneak in.
There's still a gap between DEL and SET where another client can slip in and grab the lock.

scenario: 用户一次勾选 4 个连座，要么 4 张全预留成功，要么一张都不占。
scenario_en: A user picks four adjacent seats, and it must be all four reserved or none at all.
q: 在 Redis 预留锁设计下，用户一次选择多个座位（多张票）时应该怎么抢锁？
q_en: How should the Redis lock design handle a user selecting multiple seats?
options: 给整场活动统一只设一个 key，所有座位共用同一把锁
干脆放弃 Redis 分布式锁，退回数据库行级锁去实现
所有票并行同时抢锁，谁先成功就归谁，中途失败也完全不做任何回滚
逐票顺序抢锁，失败释放已抢的锁；同节点可用 Lua 脚本做原子多锁
options_en: Use one single key for the whole event, so every seat shares that same lock.
Just drop the Redis distributed lock entirely and fall back to database row-level locking.
Grab all ticket locks in parallel, whoever succeeds first keeps it, with no rollback at all when one fails midway.
Acquire locks per ticket in sequence, release any already held on failure; same-node tickets can use a Lua script for atomic multi-lock.
why: 多票预留按票顺序抢锁，某一把失败就回滚已获得的，避免半选中；同节点场景用 Lua 脚本能把多锁获取合并成一次原子操作。
why_en: Multi-ticket bookings acquire locks one ticket at a time and roll back any already held on failure, and a Lua script can make same-node acquisition atomic.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 支持在服务端原子执行的脚本，可以把多个命令合并成一次原子操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Lua script runs atomically inside Redis, combining multiple commands into a single atomic operation.

termDefinitions.term: 哈希到同一节点 (hash to same node)
termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 集群按 key 的哈希值把数据分散到不同节点，只有落在同一节点的 key 才能用脚本原子操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis cluster shards keys across nodes by hash, and only keys landing on the same node can be scripted atomically together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要么完整执行、要么完全不执行的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic operation either completes entirely or not at all.

optionExplanations: 一把锁管全场会让任何一个用户选座都挡住其他人抢别的座位，粒度错得离谱。
退回数据库行锁会放弃 Redis 自动过期和抢锁速度这两个引入它的原因。
并行抢锁又不做失败回滚，会出现部分锁抢到、部分没抢到的半选中状态，体验很差。
每张票挨个去抢，中途哪张没抢到就把已经抢到的松开；要是这几张票恰好落在同一节点，还能借脚本把这串操作打包成一次原子调用。
optionExplanations_en: One lock for the whole event blocks any single user's seat pick from letting anyone else grab a different seat — the granularity is way off.
Falling back to database row locks gives up the two reasons Redis was introduced: auto-expiry and lock-acquisition speed.
Grabbing locks in parallel with no rollback on failure leaves users half-selected — some seats locked, some not.
Grab each ticket's lock one at a time, and let go of whatever was already acquired the moment one fails; if they land on the same node, a script can bundle the whole sequence into one atomic call.

scenario: 过期释放已经由 Redis 的 TTL 负责，数据库不该再维护第二份过期逻辑。
scenario_en: Redis TTL already handles expiry, so the database shouldn't keep a second copy of that logic.
q: 改用 Redis 分布式锁后，数据库 Ticket 表的状态简化成什么？
q_en: After moving reservation locks to Redis, what does the Ticket table status become?
options: 只剩 available 和 booked——reserved 交给 Redis 承载
available/reserved/booked 三态维持原样，一个都不动照旧保留
只剩 booked 一个状态，其余状态字段全部删掉不留
把所有状态字段统统压缩合并成一个布尔值 locked
options_en: Only available and booked remain — reserved now lives entirely inside Redis.
The three states available/reserved/booked stay exactly as they were, untouched.
Only the booked state remains; every other status field is removed.
All the status fields get collapsed together into one single boolean locked flag.
why: 预留态搬进 Redis（key=ticketId, value=userId，带 TTL），数据库只需记录 available 和 booked，过期逻辑零成本。
why_en: The reserved state moves into Redis as a keyed, TTL'd lock, so the database only needs to track available and booked, with zero-cost expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个对象在有限几个状态之间按规则转换的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state machine models an object moving between a fixed set of states under defined rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，这里用来承载临时预留状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store, here used to hold the temporary reservation state.

optionExplanations: 那个中间态被搬到别的存储去管了，数据库这边的字段就只剩「能买」和「卖出去了」两种。
三态照旧保留会让数据库还得靠 cron 或应用层逻辑处理过期，没有真正简化。
只剩 booked 一个状态没法区分「可买」和「已售」，功能不完整。
布尔值 locked 丢失了谁持有锁、何时过期这些信息，没法替代真正的状态字段。
optionExplanations_en: The middle state now lives somewhere else entirely, so the database column only has to distinguish open from sold.
Keeping all three states means the database still needs cron or application logic for expiry — nothing was actually simplified.
A single booked state can't distinguish "available" from "already sold" — the model is incomplete.
A boolean locked flag loses who holds the lock and when it expires — it can't replace a real status field.

scenario: 座位图要显示哪些座位正被别人锁着，但预留状态已经不在数据库里了。
scenario_en: The seat map still has to show which seats are held by others, but that state no longer lives in the database.
q: 预留状态搬进 Redis 后，带来的「读路径复杂度」问题是什么？
q_en: What read-path complexity appears after reservation state moves into Redis?
options: Redis 无法水平扩展，海量读请求扛不住流量
座位图要显示锁定座位，但预留状态已不在 DB 里
客户端必须直连 Redis，绕过后端服务
座位图只能整页刷新，不能局部更新座位
options_en: Redis can't scale horizontally, so massive read traffic overwhelms it.
The seat map must show locked seats, but reservation state no longer lives in the DB.
Clients must connect to Redis directly, bypassing the backend.
The seat map can only do full-page refreshes, not partial updates.
why: Event Service 渲染座位图时需要知道哪些座位被锁：查 Redis 集合多一跳但实践中很快，或把 reserved 写穿到 DB、以 Redis TTL 为过期真源。
why_en: The Event Service needs to know which seats are locked to render the seat map, so it either queries a Redis set or writes reserved status through to the database.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的集合数据结构，这里用来存某活动下所有被锁座位的 ticketId。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis Set is a collection data type, here used to hold the ticketIds locked for one event.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在写入缓存/锁的同时，把同一份状态也同步写入数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through means writing the same state into the database at the same time it's written into the cache or lock.

optionExplanations: Redis 其实很容易加节点横向扩展，这不是真正的痛点。
座位图渲染时需要知道哪些座位被锁定，但这份信息已经搬到 Redis，读路径要多打一份数据源才能拿到。
客户端直连 Redis 不是本设计的做法，绕过后端服务也不安全。
整页刷新是前端渲染方式的问题，跟预留状态搬到哪里存无关。
optionExplanations_en: Redis actually scales out easily by adding nodes — that's not the real pain point.
Rendering the seat map needs to know which seats are locked, but that data moved to Redis, so the read path needs an extra source now.
The client connecting straight to Redis isn't how this design works, and bypassing the backend service wouldn't be safe.
Full-page refresh is a frontend rendering choice, unrelated to where reservation state is stored.

scenario: Redis 锁集群整体宕机，订票接口仍然必须保证同一张票不卖两次。
scenario_en: The whole Redis lock cluster is down, and the booking endpoint still must never sell the same ticket twice.
q: 如果 Redis 锁服务整体宕机，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if the Redis lock service goes down?
options: 会立刻出现大量双重预订，系统彻底失去一致性保证
所有票会变成永久不可售状态
体验降级但不会双订：DB 的 OCC/行锁仍兜底
系统自动切换成长事务加锁模式
options_en: Lots of double bookings occur instantly and the system completely loses its consistency guarantee.
Every ticket becomes permanently unavailable.
The experience degrades but nothing double-books — the DB's OCC/row locks still back it up.
The system automatically falls back to long-running transactional locks.
why: 锁只是体验层，正确性由数据库 OCC/行锁兜底；宕机代价是用户填完支付信息才发现被抢先，比 cron 方案全场票卡死要好。
why_en: The lock is only a UX layer — correctness is backstopped by the database's OCC or row locks, so a Redis outage just means some users lose a race after entering payment info.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先不加锁地读写，提交时再检查数据是否被别人改过，冲突就让一方失败重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control lets reads/writes proceed without locking, then checks for conflicts at commit time and fails one side if data changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只锁住数据库里被访问的那一行，而不是整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A row-level lock locks only the specific row being accessed, not the whole table.

optionExplanations: 低估了数据库 OCC/行锁这道独立防线——正确性从来不靠 Redis 锁保证。
夸大了影响，实际只是无法预留而已，查看和已售票据依然正常。
用户会先感觉到卡顿或抢锁失败，但真正决定谁能买到票的判断从来不靠这层锁，所以不会出现两个人买到同一张票。
文中没有这种自动切换机制，属于凭空设想的降级路径。
optionExplanations_en: This underestimates the database's OCC/row-lock defense — correctness was never guaranteed by the Redis lock itself.
This overstates the impact — only reservation stops working; viewing and already-sold tickets keep functioning normally.
Users would feel the slowdown or a failed lock grab first, but the layer that actually decides who wins was never this lock, so nobody ends up with a duplicate ticket.
No such automatic fallback to long transactions exists in the design — this is an imagined degradation path.

scenario: 锁 TTL 是 10 分钟，用户 A 的支付卡在银行 3DS 验证上超时，B 随后抢到同一张票。
scenario_en: The lock TTL is ten minutes, user A stalls in the bank's 3-D Secure step, and user B grabs the same seat and pays.
q: 用户 A 的锁 TTL 在支付处理中途过期、用户 B 抢到锁并也付了款，怎么办？
q_en: What should happen if user A's lock expires during payment and user B also pays?
options: OCC 让一方写入失败，输家自动退款，靠放宽 TTL 加续锁去缓解
两人都能顺利成功拿到同一张票，还都以为自己抢到了
系统一检测到冲突就立刻转给人工客服排队处理协调
Redis 检测到冲突后自动把两人的两份订单悄悄合并成一笔联合订单
options_en: OCC fails one of the two writes and auto-refunds the loser, mitigated by a looser TTL plus renewing the lock.
Both users successfully end up holding the same ticket, and both think they won it.
The moment a conflict is detected, it gets routed straight to a human support agent to sort out.
On detecting a conflict, Redis automatically merges the two people's orders into one combined joint order.
why: 这种罕见竞态最终由数据库裁决：OCC 只让一个写成功，输家自动退款；工程上用宽裕 TTL、支付开始时续锁把概率压到最低。
why_en: This rare race is settled by the database — OCC lets only one write succeed and the loser gets an automatic refund, while a generous TTL plus extending the lock at payment time minimizes how often it happens.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先不加锁地读写，提交时再检查冲突，冲突就让一方失败重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control checks for conflicts at commit time and fails one side if data changed underneath it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个客户端同时操作同一份数据、结果取决于时序的场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition is when concurrent operations on shared data produce a timing-dependent outcome.

optionExplanations: 两笔写只会有一笔真正落地，另一笔自动退钱；把持有时间调宽松一点、支付一开始就续期，能让这种撞车概率降到很小。
两人都成功正是要避免的双重预订，跟需求直接矛盾。
人工介入意味着响应慢，跟线上自动化的要求不符。
Redis 只管锁，不参与订单和支付逻辑，检测到冲突也没有能力把两笔订单合并。
optionExplanations_en: Of the two writes only one actually lands and the other is auto-refunded; a looser hold time plus renewing it as soon as payment starts keeps this collision rare.
Both succeeding is exactly the double-booking this design must prevent — it contradicts the requirement outright.
Routing to a human agent means a slow response, which doesn't fit the requirement for automated, real-time handling.
Redis only manages the lock and has no part in order or payment logic, so even on a conflict it can't merge two orders.

q: 把「用 Redis 分布式锁做票预留」的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the decision chain for Redis-based ticket reservation in order.
steps: 选型：Redis 分布式锁（SET NX EX，TTL 10 分钟）
需求：结账期间临时锁票，超时要自动释放
缓解：DB 层 OCC 兜底防双订 + TTL 放宽、支付时延长锁 + 失败自动退款
决定性属性：需要自动过期 + 高并发下极快的锁操作，而 PG 没有原生行级 TTL
代价：锁服务宕机时体验降级；TTL 可能在支付中途过期
why: 完整决策链：需求（临时锁+自动释放）→ 决定性属性（自动过期、锁要快）→ 选型（Redis TTL 锁）→ 代价（宕机降级、支付中过期）→ 缓解（OCC 兜底、续锁、退款）。
why_en: The chain runs from the need for a temporary auto-releasing hold, to the deciding property of fast auto-expiry, to choosing a Redis TTL lock, to its costs, and finally to mitigating them with OCC and refunds.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子加锁命令：NX 表示 key 不存在才设置，EX 表示秒级过期时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SET with NX EX is Redis's atomic locking command, setting the key only if absent and attaching an expiry.

termDefinitions.meaning: key 的存活时间，到期自动释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the time after which a key automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 提交时检查冲突，冲突就让一方写失败重试的并发控制方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control checks for conflicts at commit time and fails one side if data changed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持事务和强一致性的关系型数据库，这里指本设计用的主数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PG (PostgreSQL) is the relational database used as the system of record here.

q: 把最终版订票流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the final booking flow in the correct order.
steps: Stripe webhook 通知支付成功，事务把 Ticket 置为 sold、Booking 置为 confirmed
用户在座位图选座，POST /bookings 携带该座位的 ticketId
Booking Service 在 Redis 抢 10 分钟 TTL 锁，并写入状态 in-progress 的 booking 记录
客户端用 Stripe.js 把卡号 token 化，携 bookingId 发起支付（服务器创建 PaymentIntent）
返回 bookingId，客户端跳转到支付页
why: 选座 → 抢 Redis 锁+写 in-progress 订单 → 返回 bookingId 进支付页 → Stripe.js 支付 → webhook 确认后落库；10 分钟内不完成，锁自动释放。
why_en: After picking a seat, the service grabs a ten-minute Redis lock and writes an in-progress booking, returns the bookingId to the payment page, then Stripe.js pays and the webhook finalizes the booking.

termDefinitions.meaning: Stripe 提供的前端 SDK，在浏览器里把银行卡信息换成一次性 token，卡号不经过我们的服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stripe.js is Stripe's browser SDK that tokenizes card details client-side so raw card numbers never reach our server.

termDefinitions.meaning: Stripe 用来跟踪一次支付全生命周期（待支付、处理中、成功、失败）的对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PaymentIntent is Stripe's object that tracks one payment's full lifecycle from pending through success or failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端事件发生后由第三方（这里是 Stripe）主动回调通知我方系统的 HTTP 请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A webhook is an HTTP callback a third party like Stripe sends to notify our system when an event happens.

termDefinitions.meaning: key 的存活时间，这里指 Redis 锁 10 分钟后自动释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the time after which the Redis lock automatically releases, here ten minutes.

scenario: 用户在支付页填写银行卡号，客户端用 Stripe.js 把卡信息换成一次性 token 再发给我们的服务器。
scenario_en: The user enters card details on the payment page; Stripe.js converts them into a one-time token before our server sees the request.
q: 为什么用 Stripe.js 在客户端做卡号 token 化？
q_en: Why use Stripe.js on the client to tokenize card numbers?
options: 为了绕过后端 Redis 分布式锁那一整套校验流程
为了让 Stripe 支付处理速度更快
为了减少客户端到服务器的一次网络请求
服务器永不接触原始卡号——这是 PCI 合规的标准做法
options_en: To bypass the backend Redis distributed lock's entire validation flow.
To make Stripe's payment processing faster.
To save one network request between client and server.
The server never touches raw card numbers — this is the standard PCI-compliance pattern.
why: Stripe.js 在浏览器端把卡信息换成 token，原始卡号不经过我们的服务器，这是 PCI 合规的标准路径；服务器只拿 token 创建 PaymentIntent。
why_en: Stripe.js tokenizes the card in the browser so the raw number never reaches our server, which is the standard PCI-compliance pattern, and the server just uses the token to create a PaymentIntent.

termDefinitions.meaning: Stripe 提供的前端 SDK，在浏览器里把银行卡信息换成一次性 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stripe.js is Stripe's browser SDK that tokenizes card details on the client side.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支付卡行业对处理银行卡信息系统的安全标准，核心是尽量少接触原始卡号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PCI compliance is the payment-card industry's security standard, whose core principle is minimizing systems that touch raw card data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把敏感的原始数据换成一个无意义的一次性标识符，原始数据本身不被传输或存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tokenization replaces sensitive raw data with a meaningless one-time identifier so the raw data itself is never transmitted or stored.

termDefinitions.meaning: Stripe 用来跟踪一次支付全生命周期的对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PaymentIntent is Stripe's object tracking one payment's full lifecycle.
