optionExplanations: Token 化和后端 Redis 锁是两套完全无关的机制，跟绕过锁校验流程没有关系。
Token 化不会改变 Stripe 内部的处理速度，速度不是它的目的。
Token 化其实还多了一次浏览器到 Stripe 的请求，并没有减少网络往返。
原始卡号只在浏览器和 Stripe 之间流转，服务器永不接触，这是 PCI 合规的标准做法，也大幅缩小了服务器的合规范围。
optionExplanations_en: Tokenization and the backend Redis lock are two entirely unrelated mechanisms — it has nothing to do with bypassing lock checks.
Tokenization doesn't change Stripe's internal processing speed — speed isn't its purpose.
Tokenization actually adds an extra browser-to-Stripe request, not fewer round trips.
The raw card number only ever flows between browser and Stripe, never touching the server — the standard PCI-compliant path, shrinking compliance scope.

scenario: Stripe 处理完支付后会调用我们的 webhook 通知结果；网络失败或超时时，Stripe 会对同一个事件重试投递。
scenario_en: After payment, Stripe calls our webhook, and it may retry the same event after a timeout or network failure.
q: 为什么 webhook 处理器必须幂等，怎么实现？
q_en: Why must the webhook handler be idempotent, and how do you implement that?
options: 因为 webhook 走的是明文 HTTP 传输、内容未加密，要靠 TLS 加密协议来解决
Stripe 重试会导致同一事件被处理两次；用 bookingId 做幂等键，更新前先查状态
因为 Redis 锁服务出故障后会不停重复广播过期事件出去
幂等处理只是锦上添花的一个可选优化项，不做也完全不影响正确性
options_en: Because webhooks travel over plaintext HTTP with their contents unencrypted, so TLS encryption is the fix needed.
Stripe's retries can process the same event twice; use bookingId as the idempotency key and check status before updating.
Because the Redis lock service, after a failure, keeps rebroadcasting the same lapsing key event over and over.
Idempotency is just a nice-to-have optional extra, and skipping it doesn't affect correctness at all.
why: Stripe 对失败的 webhook 会重试；不幂等的处理器可能让同一笔支付触发两次状态变更。用 bookingId 做幂等键、更新前先查当前状态，让重试变安全。
why_en: Stripe retries webhooks on failure, so a non-idempotent handler could apply the same payment's state change twice, which is why bookingId is used as the idempotency key with a status check before updating.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第三方系统（这里是 Stripe）在事件发生后主动回调通知我方服务器的 HTTP 请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A webhook is an HTTP callback a third party like Stripe sends to notify our server when an event occurs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个操作重复执行多次，结果和只执行一次完全一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotent operation produces the same result whether it runs once or is retried multiple times.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加密网络传输的协议，防止数据被窃听或篡改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS is a protocol that encrypts network traffic to prevent eavesdropping or tampering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识一次操作唯一性的键，用它检查该操作是否已经执行过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key uniquely identifies one operation so you can check whether it has already been applied.

optionExplanations: TLS 解决的是传输窃听问题，跟同一事件被重复处理没有关系。
上游那边送达失败了会再送一次，收到方如果没有去重手段，两次投递可能把状态改动执行两遍。
过期事件的广播和 webhook 重试完全是两套机制，没有关联。
不做幂等时，重试会把同一笔支付的状态改两次，这不是可选项而是必须处理的正确性问题。
optionExplanations_en: TLS solves eavesdropping in transit, unrelated to the same event being processed twice.
The sender resends on a failed delivery, and without a dedupe check on the receiving end, two deliveries can trigger the same state change twice.
Broadcasting expiring keys and webhook retries are two completely separate mechanisms with no connection.
Without idempotency, a retry would apply the same payment's status change twice — a correctness requirement, not an optional extra.

scenario: 结账要填写支付信息通常需要几分钟；热门演唱会里，同一座位常有大量用户同时排队抢同一把锁。
scenario_en: Checkout takes several minutes, while many users may compete for the same seat at a hot concert.
q: 预留锁的 TTL 时长该由什么权衡决定？
q_en: What tradeoff should set the reservation-lock TTL?
options: 设得很长，比如整整 1 小时，给填卡慢的用户留出充裕缓冲
设在大约 10 分钟量级：够完成支付，又不会让热门票占太久
设为 1 秒，让票几乎立刻回到可售池，几乎不给用户留时间
干脆永不过期，只靠人工手动释放，很容易被人遗忘处理
options_en: Set it very long, a full hour, to give slow typers a generous buffer.
Set it around ten minutes: enough to finish paying without hogging hot seats too long.
Set it to one second so the ticket returns to the pool almost immediately, barely any grace period.
Skip automatic release entirely and rely on staff to free it by hand, which is easy to forget.
why: TTL 太短会让正常用户来不及付款就掉单；太长会让热门场次的票被一个人攥住太久，拉低所有人的可用性——10 分钟左右是两者的折中，支付发起时还能续锁。
why_en: Too short a TTL drops honest buyers mid-checkout, while too long a TTL locks popular seats away from everyone else, so something around ten minutes balances the two, with the option to extend it once payment starts.

termDefinitions.meaning: key 的存活时间，这里指预留锁自动释放前能持有多久。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a key is held before it automatically expires, here the reservation lock's hold time.

optionExplanations: 1 小时确实给足了填卡时间，但热门场次里这张票会被一个人白占快一小时，其他排队的人根本抢不到。
10 分钟左右卡在够用户填完支付、又不让票被占太久这两条线中间，真要更久还能在支付发起那一刻续锁。
1 秒钟连正常人切个信用卡 app 都做不完，还没输完卡号锁就没了，等于没给出预留窗口。
没有自动释放兜底，一旦运营没及时手动清，票就会一直被挂起卖不出去。
optionExplanations_en: A full hour does give plenty of time to fill in card details, but at a hot show that one ticket sits locked away from everyone else in line for nearly an hour.
Around ten minutes sits between giving buyers enough time to pay and not tying up a hot ticket too long, and it can still be renewed once payment starts.
One second doesn't even survive switching to a card app, so the hold vanishes before the buyer finishes typing a card number — no real reservation window.
With no automatic release as a backstop, a ticket stays stuck unsellable the moment staff forget to clear it by hand.

scenario: 抢票开售时活动页被打爆：成千上万用户反复刷新同一个活动页等票放出，读流量是写的百倍。
scenario_en: During a ticket drop, thousands of users keep refreshing the same event page, and reads outnumber writes by about 100 to 1.
q: 最该激进缓存的数据是？
q_en: Which data should be cached most aggressively?
options: 实时座位预留状态
支付交易流水
活动详情与场馆信息
用户会话令牌
why: 决定性约束是读多改少：活动和场馆信息几乎不变，能放心猛缓存；座位状态秒级变化，不适合久缓存。
why_en: Cache the event and venue data hard because it is read constantly but almost never changes, while seat status shifts by the second and cannot be cached for long.
whenOtherWins: 冷门场次座位变化慢、能容忍秒级陈旧时，给座位状态加短 TTL 缓存也可接受；爆款场次必须走实时推送。
tradeoff: 静态活动信息的缓存命中率 vs 座位状态缓存带来的陈旧风险
options_en: Cache real-time seat reservation status.
Cache payment transaction records.
Cache event and venue details.
Cache user session tokens.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cached entry stays valid before it must be refreshed.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器通过一条持久连接单向推送数据给客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push updates to a client over one persistent, one-way connection.

optionExplanations: 座位状态秒级变化，缓存了也很快失效，还容易让用户看到旧座位——只有能容忍短暂陈旧时才适合缓存。
支付流水跟这次读风暴无关，缓存它不解决刷新流量的压力。
活动和场馆信息几乎不变，读多改少，正是刷新流量的真正瓶颈，缓存收益最大。
会话令牌跟活动读取压力无关，不是这次要缓解的热点数据。
optionExplanations_en: Seat status changes second by second, so a cache goes stale fast and risks showing a taken seat as open — only worth it when brief staleness is fine.
Payment transaction records are unrelated to this read storm; caching them doesn't relieve the refresh pressure.
Event and venue details barely change and are read far more than written — the actual bottleneck behind the refresh traffic, so caching pays off most.
Session tokens are unrelated to event-read load — they're not the hot data causing this pressure.

scenario: 开售时同一场活动的详情页 QPS 打到数万，数据在几分钟内几乎不变。
scenario_en: At on-sale one event page takes tens of thousands of requests per second while its data barely changes for minutes.
q: 给 Ticketmaster 活动详情做读路径缓存，键值设计和读取策略该怎么定？
q_en: For Ticketmaster event-detail caching, how should you choose the key and read strategy?
options: SQL 语句本身当 key
eventId 当 key
整份数据库快照当缓存
只缓存静态图片
why: 以 eventId 为 key 缓存整个活动对象，命中直接返回；read-through 保证未命中时自动查库回填，靠内存速度扛住大量读。
why_en: Key the cache by eventId so a hit returns the whole event object directly, and use a read-through strategy so a miss automatically queries the database and backfills the cache.
options_en: Use the raw SQL statement as the key.
Use eventId as the key.
Cache a full snapshot of the database.
Cache only static images.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存未命中时由缓存层自动查库并回填，业务代码不用单独处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In a read-through cache, a miss automatically triggers a database read and fills the cache, with no extra code in the application.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见的内存型 key-value 缓存服务，读写速度远快于磁盘数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis and Memcached are in-memory key-value stores that read and write far faster than a disk-backed database.

optionExplanations: 把可变的查询语句字符串当 key，同一活动的等价查询写法不同就会各占一份缓存，命中率很差。
拿活动本身的唯一标识当缓存的入口，同一场活动不管谁来查都命中同一份，后端压力才真正被挡住。
把整份数据库塞进缓存，内存占用和数据库体量绑死，规模一大就扛不住。
只缓存静态图片没有覆盖活动详情这类结构化高频读数据，没解决真正的读压力。
optionExplanations_en: Using the mutable SQL string as the key means equivalent queries written differently each get their own cache entry — hit rate suffers.
Use the event's own unique identifier as the cache entry, so every lookup for that event hits the same slot and the backend actually gets shielded.
Stuffing the entire database into cache ties memory footprint to database size — it can't scale.
Caching only static images misses the structured, high-frequency event-detail reads, so it doesn't solve the real read pressure.

scenario: 活动详情被缓存后，主办方随时可能改期换阵容，而余票数每秒都在变。
scenario_en: Event details are cached, but organizers can reschedule or swap performers at any time and remaining-ticket counts change every second.
q: Ticketmaster 活动详情缓存，怎么保证失效和一致性？
q_en: How should Ticketmaster keep event-detail cache invalidation and consistency under control?
options: 数据库触发器在改期换阵容时精确通知失效，配合分层 TTL 兜底
什么自动机制都不做，全靠运维人工发现问题后再手动清理缓存条目
缓存条目永不主动失效，只有服务重启才会被清空刷新
每一次写入操作都无差别地清空整个缓存全部内容
why: 双保险保证一致性：DB 触发器在改期、换阵容时精确失效对应条目；分层 TTL 兜底——静态数据长 TTL，余票类数据短 TTL。
why_en: Consistency comes from two layers: a database trigger precisely invalidates the affected entry on changes like a date or lineup update, while tiered TTLs act as a backstop with long TTLs for static data and short TTLs for fast-changing data.
options_en: A database trigger precisely signals invalidation on date/lineup changes, backed by tiered TTLs as a fallback.
Do nothing automated at all — rely entirely on ops staff noticing and manually clearing cache entries.
Cache entries never lapse on their own; only a server restart ever clears them out.
Every single write, without exception, wipes out the entire cache's contents.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cached entry stays valid before it must be refreshed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据变更时数据库自动触发的回调，可用来通知缓存失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A database trigger fires automatically on a data change and can be used to notify the cache to invalidate an entry.

optionExplanations: 数据一变就有信号主动清掉对应条目，不用等 TTL 到点；不同字段再按更新频率分开设过期时长兜底。
人工响应慢，抢票期间数据一变，很难被运维及时发现并清理。
永不失效会让用户在活动改期后一直看到旧信息，直到下次重启才刷新。
热门活动写操作一多，每次都清空整份缓存等于反复打空，失去缓存的意义。
optionExplanations_en: A change fires a signal that clears just the affected entry right away instead of waiting on a timer, with per-field TTLs as a fallback based on how often each changes.
Manual clearing is too slow — during a ticket rush, changed data often isn't caught and cleared in time by ops.
Never expiring means users keep seeing stale info after a reschedule until the next server restart.
Wiping the entire cache on every write, during heavy-write events, effectively defeats the purpose of caching.

scenario: Event 与 Search 服务各扩到几十个实例，流量必须均匀落到每个实例上。
scenario_en: Event and Search each run dozens of instances, and traffic has to spread evenly across all of them.
q: Ticketmaster 把 Event Service、Search Service 都横向扩展后，负载均衡该怎么用？
q_en: How should load balancing be used after horizontally scaling Event Service and Search Service?
options: 只在数据库前需要
用一致性哈希是唯一选择
所有横向扩展的组件前都配负载均衡
负载均衡会破坏数据库事务一致性
why: 所有横向扩展的组件（服务和数据库）前都要有负载均衡；Round Robin 或 Least Connections 把流量摊匀到各实例，面试图里常省略但值得口头提。
why_en: Every horizontally scaled component, service or database, needs a load balancer in front of it, typically using round robin or least connections to spread traffic evenly across instances.
options_en: Only the database needs one.
Consistent hashing is the only valid algorithm.
Every horizontally scaled component gets a load balancer.
Load balancing breaks database transaction consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轮询算法，按顺序把请求依次分给每台实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round robin sends each new request to the next server in a fixed rotation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把新请求分给当前连接数最少的实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Least connections routes each new request to the server currently handling the fewest active connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按哈希环分配请求或数据的算法，常用于分片或缓存路由，不是通用负载均衡算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps requests or data onto a hash ring and is mainly used for sharding or cache routing, not general load balancing.

optionExplanations: 只在数据库前配 LB 会让 Event/Search/Booking 这些服务实例前没有分流，流量堆到某几个实例上。
一致性哈希是分片或缓存路由的工具，不是唯一的负载均衡算法，把两者搞混了。
凡是横向扩出多个实例的东西，前面都得有个东西替它分流量，不管它是服务还是数据库。
负载均衡只管流量分发，不影响数据库事务的一致性保证，两者互不干扰。
optionExplanations_en: Putting a load balancer only in front of the database leaves Event/Search/Booking instances unbalanced — traffic piles onto a few.
Consistent hashing is a tool for sharding or cache routing, not the only load-balancing algorithm — the two are conflated.
Anything scaled out to multiple instances — service or database alike — needs something in front spreading traffic across them.
Load balancing only handles traffic distribution; it doesn't affect the database's transactional consistency guarantee.

scenario: 要靠加机器扛住开售读风暴，扩容不能要求请求粘在固定实例上。
scenario_en: You need to absorb the on-sale read storm by adding machines, and that only works if requests are not pinned to one instance.
q: Ticketmaster 的 Event Service 为什么可以随意横向扩展？
q_en: Why can Ticketmaster's Event Service scale horizontally so easily?
options: 因为它用了最快的编程语言
因为它不需要连数据库
因为它跑在 Kubernetes 上
因为它是无状态服务
why: 决定性原因是无状态：实例不保存本地会话或数据，任何请求可以落到任何实例，所以加机器加负载均衡就能线性扩容。
why_en: Event Service can scale horizontally at will because it is stateless, so any instance can serve any request once you add more machines behind a load balancer.
options_en: Because it is written in the fastest programming language.
Because it never needs to query a database.
Because it runs on Kubernetes.
Because it is a stateless service.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务实例不在本地保存会话或业务状态，任何实例都能处理任何请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stateless service keeps no local session or business state, so any instance can handle any request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过增加更多实例（而不是升级单机配置）来承接更多流量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling means adding more instances, rather than upgrading a single machine, to handle more traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种容器编排平台，负责部署和管理服务实例，本身不是扩展能力的来源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kubernetes is a container orchestration platform that deploys and manages service instances, but it is not itself the source of scalability.

optionExplanations: 语言快慢不影响能不能开多个实例分流量，这不是能横向扩展的原因。
它其实要查 Events DB 拿事件、场馆、表演者数据，这个「不查库」的前提是错的。
换成裸机或别的编排方式一样能横向扩展，跟具体用不用 K8s 无关。
实例不在本地保存任何用户或会话状态，任何请求可以落到任何实例，加机器加负载均衡就能线性扩容。
optionExplanations_en: Language speed doesn't affect whether you can spin up more instances to share load — it's not the reason it scales.
It actually needs to query the Events DB for event, venue, and performer data — the "doesn't touch the database" premise is wrong.
It would scale out the same way on bare metal or any other orchestrator — it has nothing specifically to do with Kubernetes.
Instances hold no local user or session state, so any request can land on any instance — adding machines scales it linearly.

scenario: 缓存加横向扩展方案上线后，面试官追问它留下了哪些真实成本。
scenario_en: After proposing caching plus horizontal scaling, the interviewer asks what real costs that combination leaves behind.
q: Ticketmaster 用「缓存 + 横向扩展」应对读风暴，这套方案真实存在的挑战有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What real challenges remain with caching plus horizontal scaling for read storms?
options: 缓存与数据库一致性维护，活动详情频繁变更时更棘手
大量服务实例的部署与回滚运维复杂度
引入缓存后系统自动获得强一致性，不用再处理
无状态服务本身没法通过加实例来扩容
why: 两大真实挑战：缓存与数据库的一致性维护、实例膨胀后的部署与回滚运维复杂度。缓存不会自动带来强一致，无状态服务也不会因扩容变差。
why_en: The two real challenges are keeping the cache consistent with the database and managing the operational complexity of deploying and rolling back many instances, since caching never grants automatic strong consistency and statelessness is what makes scaling safe.
options_en: Cache-database consistency gets harder if event details change often.
Deploying and rolling back many instances adds operational complexity.
Adding a cache automatically gives the system strong consistency.
A stateless service cannot actually be scaled by adding instances.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任何时刻读到的数据都和最近一次写入完全一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency means every read reflects the most recent write immediately.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务实例不在本地保存会话或业务状态，任何实例都能处理任何请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stateless service keeps no local session or business state, so any instance can handle any request.

optionExplanations: 缓存内容和数据库真实值可能出现短暂不一致，活动详情频繁变更时这个风险更棘手。
抢票期间实例数量会很多，发布新版本和出问题时的回滚都变得更复杂。
缓存本身不解决一致性，写库和失效之间总有窗口期，这是常见的误解。
无状态恰恰是能任意加实例的原因，这个说法把因果关系搞反了。
optionExplanations_en: Cached content can briefly diverge from the true database value, and this gets thornier when event details change often.
During a ticket rush, instance counts spike, making rollouts and rollbacks noticeably more complex.
Caching by itself doesn't grant strong consistency — there's always a window between a write and its invalidation.
Statelessness is exactly why instances can be added freely — this claim has the causality backwards.

scenario: 热门活动的座位图很快过时：用户反复点到已被订走的座位而沮丧，需要不刷新页面就同步座位状态。
scenario_en: Hot-event seat maps go stale quickly; users need seat status updates without refreshing the page.
q: 推荐的实时更新方案是？
q_en: What real-time update approach should the seat map use?
options: 客户端每 30 秒整页刷新
SSE 服务器单向推送
客户端定时轮询
让用户手动点刷新按钮
why: 只需要服务器把座位变化推给客户端，不需要客户端上行。SSE 用一条持久连接做到这点，比轮询省资源、比 WebSocket 简单。
why_en: Since seat updates only need to flow from server to client, SSE delivers that over one persistent connection more simply than polling and with less overhead than WebSocket.
whenOtherWins: 未来若需要客户端主动上行（比如实时协同选座），才该换成双向的 WebSocket。
tradeoff: 服务器推送的实时性 vs 轮询/整页刷新的实现简单度
options_en: The client does a full page refresh every 30 seconds.
SSE: one-way server-to-client push.
The client polls on a fixed interval.
Rely on the user manually clicking refresh.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器通过一条长连接单向推送数据给客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to a client over one long-lived, one-way connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端按固定间隔主动发请求查询最新状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polling means the client repeatedly sends requests at a fixed interval to check for updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that supports two-way message exchange between client and server over a single connection.

optionExplanations: 30 秒间隔内座位状态仍可能是错的，体验没有本质改善，只在能接受这个粒度的陈旧时才凑合。
信息只往一个方向走，客户端不用往回发东西，用一条常开连接接着就行，比反复问一遍轻，也比双向协议简单。
轮询间隔越短服务器压力越大，越长越不实时，两头都难兼顾。
把同步责任推给用户，大部分人根本不会主动点，只适合极低频、可容忍延迟的场景。
optionExplanations_en: Seat status can still be wrong within a 30-second window — no real improvement, only tolerable if that staleness is acceptable.
The data only ever flows one way and the client never needs to talk back, so a single always-open connection covers it — lighter than re-asking and simpler than a two-way protocol.
Shorter polling intervals strain the server, longer ones feel stale — there's no good middle ground.
Pushing sync responsibility onto users means most won't bother clicking — only fits very low-frequency, delay-tolerant cases.

scenario: Taylor Swift 场次开售：百万人盯着同一张 6 万座的座位图，票在几秒内被抢光。
scenario_en: A Taylor Swift on-sale: a million people stare at the same 60,000-seat map and everything sells out within seconds.
q: SSE（服务器单向推送）座位图，在「Taylor Swift 级」活动会出什么问题？
q_en: What goes wrong with an SSE seat map during a Taylor Swift-scale event?
options: SSE 连接数有硬上限 100
SSE 会导致双重预订
浏览器不支持 SSE
座位秒光，用户体验混乱失控
why: SSE 技术上完全正确地推送了座位变化，但千万人抢一场时座位几秒内被抢光，实时更新反而放大了混乱——这是业务问题，不是技术故障。
why_en: SSE technically pushes every seat update correctly, but when millions compete for the same show, seats vanish within seconds and the real-time updates just amplify the chaos instead of fixing it.
options_en: SSE has a hard cap of 100 connections.
SSE causes double bookings.
Browsers do not support SSE.
Seats vanish in seconds, and the UX spirals into chaos.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器通过持久连接单向推送更新给客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is a mechanism where a server pushes updates to a client over a persistent one-way connection.

optionExplanations: SSE 连接数由服务器内存和文件描述符决定：单机 ≈ 数万连接，协议本身没有 100 这个上限。
双重预订由数据库事务和锁保证，SSE 只负责推送通知，跟双订没有关系。
主流浏览器都原生支持 SSE，兼容性不是这里的瓶颈。
推送没出岔子：百万观众 × 6 万座位 = 每个座位上百人争抢，座位存量比消息更快耗尽，场面就乱了。
optionExplanations_en: SSE connection limits come from server memory and file descriptors — roughly tens of thousands per box — not a hardcoded 100 in the protocol.
Double-booking is prevented by database transactions and locks — SSE only handles push notifications.
All major browsers natively support SSE, so compatibility isn't the bottleneck here.
Nothing breaks in the push — a million viewers against sixty thousand seats means hundreds of people per seat, so inventory burns out faster than any message can report it.

scenario: 千万用户同时抢同一场演出，直接放所有人进选座页会压垮系统且体验混乱。
scenario_en: Tens of millions of users hitting one concert at once would overload seat selection and create a chaotic experience.
q: 该用什么机制控制用户涌入选座页的节奏？
q_en: What mechanism should control how users enter the seat-selection page?
options: 无限加服务器硬扛峰值流量
临时关闭座位图
管理员启用的虚拟等待队列
随机丢弃部分请求
why: 虚拟等待室在用户看到选座页之前就把人排队，按节奏放行，把不可控的瞬时峰值拉平成可控流量。这是「最好的解法不一定更难」的例子。
why_en: A virtual waiting room queues users before they ever reach the seat map, admitting them at a controlled pace instead of absorbing an uncontrollable spike all at once.
whenOtherWins: 热度没到「秒光」级别时，SSE 实时推送座位图就够用，不必启用排队。
tradeoff: 可控节奏放行 vs 直接放全部人进导致系统过载
options_en: Keep adding servers to brute-force the peak traffic.
Temporarily disable the seat map.
An admin-enabled virtual waiting queue.
Randomly drop some incoming requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器主动向客户端单向推送更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is a mechanism where the server pushes updates to the client over a one-way connection.

optionExplanations: 千万级瞬时并发下加多少机器都可能被打穿，还很烧钱，只在流量可预测且预算充足时才行得通。
临时关闭座位图等于放弃这单生意，用户体验反而更差，只在系统真扛不住的极端情况下才是权宜之计。
让人先在页面外候着，系统按自己的节奏一批批放人进来，冲进来的洪峰就变成了一条可控的细水流。
随机丢弃请求让谁被丢、谁能进全凭运气，公平性和体验都很差，只在没有更好机制时才是无奈之选。
optionExplanations_en: At tens-of-millions concurrency, adding machines can still get overwhelmed and it's expensive — only works with predictable traffic and generous budget.
Taking the seat map offline temporarily gives up the sale entirely, worse for users — only a last resort when the system truly can't cope.
Hold people outside the page first and let the system admit them in controlled batches, turning an unmanageable rush into a steady, controllable trickle.
Randomly dropping requests makes admission a coin flip — poor on fairness and experience, only acceptable absent a better mechanism.

scenario: 开售瞬间百万人涌入，必须按先来后到放行，并让每个人看到自己的实时排位。
scenario_en: A million people arrive at once, admission must be first-come-first-served, and everyone should see their live position.
q: Ticketmaster 抢票用的虚拟等待队列，技术实现该怎么做？
q_en: How should the virtual waiting queue be implemented for Ticketmaster?
options: Redis sorted set 记分排序 + 持久连接实时推送排位变化
Kafka 存队列消息，靠定时发送邮件逐个通知用户去查看自己当前的排位
用普通数据库表存队列数据，让客户端定时轮询反复去查询
客户端本地跑一个倒计时计时器，时间到了就自己放行进入
why: sorted set 用进入时间当分数天然维持先来后到；持久连接（SSE 或 WebSocket）把排位变化实时推给用户，不用轮询查库。
why_en: A Redis sorted set keeps first-come-first-served order by using the enqueue timestamp as the score, while a persistent connection pushes position updates without repeated polling.
options_en: A Redis sorted set scores entries for ordering, plus a persistent connection pushing live position updates.
Store the queue in Kafka and periodically email each user to go check their current position.
Store the queue in a plain database table and have the client poll it on a fixed interval.
Run a local countdown timer on the client and let it admit the user on its own once time's up.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合数据结构，每个成员带一个分数并按分数自动排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sorted set is a Redis data structure where every member has a score and the set stays ordered by that score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开、可以持续推送数据的连接，如 SSE 或 WebSocket。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A persistent connection stays open between client and server so the server can keep pushing data, as with SSE or WebSocket.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息队列/流处理平台，擅长高吞吐顺序写入，但不是按分数排序取值的数据结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging and stream-processing platform built for high-throughput ordered writes, not for score-ranked lookups.

optionExplanations: 用进队时刻当排序依据，谁先来天然排前面；配一条常开连接把名次变化实时推出去，省掉了反复查库这一步。
Kafka 不天然支持按分数取队首，定时邮件的延迟也跟不上秒级排位变化。
普通表存队列、客户端定时查询，在千万级排队场景下会把数据库打垮。
客户端本地状态不可信，谁都能改本地代码作弊插队。
optionExplanations_en: Score each entry by arrival time so first-come naturally sorts first, and pair it with an always-open connection pushing rank changes live instead of repeated polling.
Kafka doesn't naturally support fetching the head by score, and periodic email latency can't keep up with second-by-second position changes.
A plain table with clients polling would crush the database at tens-of-millions-of-users queue scale.
Client-side local state can't be trusted — anyone can edit local code to cheat their way up the queue.

scenario: 等待队列已上线，但用户完全可以绕过前端直接构造请求打 Booking 接口。
scenario_en: The waiting queue is live, but a user can skip the UI and call the booking endpoint directly.
q: 在虚拟等待队列前提下，怎么防止用户绕过排队直接调 Booking 接口？
q_en: With a virtual waiting queue, how do you stop users from bypassing it and calling Booking directly?
options: 只在前端隐藏按钮
写入带 TTL 的准入集合
给每个用户发一次性准入链接
技术上无法防止
why: 放行是服务端状态：dequeue 时把用户会话 ID 写进带 TTL 的 admitted:{eventId} 集合，Booking Service 受理请求前先查这个集合，绕过前端也没用。
why_en: Admission is server-side state: when a user is dequeued, their session ID is added to a TTL-bound admitted set, and the Booking Service checks that set before accepting any request, so skipping the front end does not help.
options_en: Only hide the button in the front end.
Write to a TTL-bound admitted set.
Send each user a one-time admission link.
It technically cannot be prevented.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集合里这条准入记录的存活时间，过期后自动失去放行资格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Here TTL is how long an admission record stays valid before it automatically expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端维护的、记录哪些用户已被放行可以订票的集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The admitted set is server-side state that records which users have been let through the queue and may book.

optionExplanations: 前端代码用户可以直接改，隐藏按钮挡不住直接调用接口。
真正拦人的不是界面，是后端一份带过期时间的名单：出队那刻把会话记进去，下单前先查这份名单在不在。
一次性链接一旦泄露或被转发，一次性属性就形同虚设，人人可用。
服务端状态完全能做到准入控制，这个判断本身是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Frontend code is user-editable — hiding a button doesn't stop a direct API call.
What actually blocks people isn't the UI — it's a server-side list with an expiry; the session gets added the moment it's dequeued, and booking checks that list before proceeding.
A one-time link stops being one-time the moment it leaks or gets forwarded — anyone with it can use it.
Server-side state can absolutely enforce admission control — this claim is simply wrong.

scenario: 排位变化只需要服务器往客户端推，客户端在等待期间不需要回传任何数据。
scenario_en: Queue-position updates only flow server to client; the browser sends nothing back while waiting.
q: 「通信方向」维度上，SSE（服务器推送）和 WebSocket（双向）有什么区别？
q_en: On communication direction, how do SSE and WebSocket differ?
options: SSE 单向服务器推送；WebSocket 双向
SSE 双向通信、WebSocket 只能单向
两者都只能客户端到服务器
两者完全等价
why: SSE 只走服务器到客户端单向、协议更轻；WebSocket 支持双向但握手和维护更重。排位推送只需要下行，所以选 SSE。
why_en: SSE only pushes from server to client and stays lightweight, while WebSocket supports two-way communication at the cost of a heavier handshake, so a one-way feed like queue-position updates fits SSE better.
tradeoff: 单向推送的轻量 vs 双向通信的灵活性
options_en: SSE is one-way server push; WebSocket is two-way.
SSE is bidirectional and WebSocket can only go one way.
Both only go from client to server.
The two are completely equivalent.

termDefinitions.meaning: Server-Sent Events，服务器通过一条持久连接单向推送数据给客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE is a protocol where the server pushes data to the client over one persistent, one-way connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个连接上支持客户端和服务器双向收发消息的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol that supports two-way message exchange between client and server over a single connection.

optionExplanations: 一个只能从服务器发到客户端，另一个两头都能发；既然排位信息只用往下发，选轻的那个就够了。
把方向关系说反了，按这个理解选型会直接选错协议。
两者其实都支持服务器主动推送，「都只能客户端到服务器」这个前提是错的。
两者在通信方向上并不等价，认为没区别会让人忽略 WebSocket 多出的双向能力和额外开销。
optionExplanations_en: One can only go from server to client, the other can carry traffic both ways; since rank updates only ever need to go down, the lighter one is enough.
This reverses the actual direction — building on this would pick the wrong protocol outright.
Both actually support server-initiated push, so "only client-to-server" is simply wrong.
The two aren't equivalent in direction — treating them as the same ignores WebSocket's extra bidirectional overhead.

scenario: 百万人排队、平均等待 20 分钟，最大的流失恰恰发生在等待过程中。
scenario_en: A million people queue for twenty minutes on average, and most of the drop-off happens while they wait.
q: 虚拟等待队列上线后，最大的体验风险和缓解手段是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest UX risk after launching a virtual waiting queue, and how do you reduce it?
options: 队列会在崩溃时丢数据，靠 Kafka 持久化解决
用户会拿到重复座位，靠加锁解决
队列耗尽内存，靠换数据库解决
等待过久引发沮丧，靠持续推送排位与预计等待时间缓解
why: 等待室的风险不在技术在心理：不透明或不准的等待最伤体验。持久连接本来就开着，用它持续推排位和预计等待时间，把不确定感降到最低。
why_en: The waiting room's real risk is psychological, not technical: inaccurate or opaque wait times hurt the experience most, so the same persistent connection is used to keep pushing position and ETA updates.
options_en: The queue loses data on a crash, fixed by persisting it in Kafka.
Users get duplicate seats, fixed by adding locks.
The queue exhausts memory, fixed by switching databases.
Long waits cause frustration, mitigated by pushing live position and ETA.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持打开、可持续推送数据的连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A persistent connection stays open between client and server so updates can keep streaming.

optionExplanations: sorted set 加持久化本来就不易丢数据，崩溃丢数据不是本题的真实风险。
重复座位由 Booking Service 的数据库事务和锁保证，不归排队机制管。
sorted set 存的是排队记录，量级远达不到耗尽内存。
等待室的风险在心理不在技术：预计等待不准或队伍变慢时用户会觉得被晾在一边，持续推送排位和预计时间能把不确定感降到最低。
optionExplanations_en: A persisted sorted set doesn't easily lose data even on a crash — that's not the real risk here.
Duplicate seats are prevented by Booking Service's database transactions and locks, not by the queue mechanism.
The sorted set only holds queue records, nowhere near enough volume to exhaust memory.
The waiting room's risk is psychological, not technical: an inaccurate ETA makes users feel abandoned — continuous position/ETA pushes minimize that.

scenario: Ticketmaster 要求搜索延迟 <500ms，且活动数量还在持续增长，这条关键字过滤 SQL 是当前实现。
scenario_en: Ticketmaster needs search under 500ms, event count keeps growing, and this SQL keyword filter is the current implementation.
q: 这条搜索查询为什么慢？
q_en: Why is this search query slow?
options: 前导 %通配符% 让 B-tree 索引完全失效，只能整表扫描，活动越多越慢
OR 条件天生就比 AND 慢上很多，写查询时应该尽量避免使用它
问题出在 SELECT * 这个写法上，只要少选几个不用的字段查询就会变快
Events 表缺少一个主键字段，导致索引结构根本没能生效工作
why: 前导 %Taylor% 让普通 B-tree 索引用不上，只能整表扫描；活动数量越涨，这条路径越撑不住 <500ms 的延迟要求。
why_en: A leading wildcard defeats a standard B-tree index and forces a full table scan that only gets slower as the event catalog grows.
codeSample:
-- 慢查询：前置通配符无法走 B-tree 索引
SELECT *
FROM Events
WHERE name LIKE '%Taylor%'
   OR description LIKE '%Taylor%';
options_en: A leading %wildcard% completely defeats the B-tree index, forcing a full table scan that gets slower as events grow.
OR is inherently much slower than AND, so it should be avoided whenever writing a query.
The real problem is the SELECT * syntax; selecting a few fewer unused columns would make it faster.
The Events table is missing a primary key field, which is why the index never actually kicks in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按排序结构组织的数据库索引，擅长等值和前缀匹配查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree index is a sorted index structure that is efficient for equality and prefix lookups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 像 %Taylor% 这样把 % 放在开头的匹配模式，数据库无法用索引定位起点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A leading wildcard, like %Taylor%, puts the % at the start of the pattern, so the database cannot use an index to find a starting point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库逐行检查整张表来找匹配行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full table scan checks every row in a table one by one to find matches.

optionExplanations: 关键词前面带了通配符，索引没法从头对起，只能一行行比对，活动一多这条路就越走越慢。
OR 本身不是这条查询慢的原因，把它当成性能杀手是常见误解。
去掉 SELECT * 顶多省一点带宽，扫描方式没有变化，不解决根本问题。
本例的主键与索引失效无关，缺主键不是这条查询变慢的原因。
optionExplanations_en: Putting a wildcard before the keyword gives the index nothing to anchor on, so it falls back to checking row after row, and that gets worse as events pile up.
OR itself isn't why this query is slow — treating it as a performance killer is a common misconception.
Dropping SELECT * saves a bit of bandwidth at most; the scan pattern doesn't change.
A missing primary key is unrelated to the index failing here — that's not why this query slowed down.

scenario: 搜索延迟要求 <500ms，第一步先在现有 Postgres 上做基础优化，暂不引入新组件。
scenario_en: Search must stay under 500ms; first optimize the existing Postgres path without adding a new component.
q: Good 级方案是？
q_en: What is the Good-level search optimization?
options: 直接引入 Elasticsearch 集群
给常用搜索列建索引，并优化查询语句
把数据库整体换成 NoSQL
把搜索过滤逻辑放到前端做
why: 先给常用搜索列建索引减少扫描行数，再用 EXPLAIN、避免 SELECT *、LIMIT、UNION 替代 OR 做查询优化——这是不引入新组件的第一步。
why_en: The first step is indexing the frequently searched columns and tuning queries with EXPLAIN, narrower SELECTs, LIMIT, and UNION instead of OR.
whenOtherWins: 需要部分匹配、错别字容忍或复杂排序时，普通索引不够，该升级到全文索引或 Elasticsearch。
tradeoff: 索引+查询优化 vs 引入 Elasticsearch 这类新搜索组件
options_en: Stand up an Elasticsearch cluster right away.
Index the common search columns and tune the queries.
Replace the whole database with a NoSQL store.
Push search filtering to the front end.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库为加速查找而维护的辅助结构，用列值映射到行位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An index is an auxiliary structure a database maintains to speed up lookups by mapping column values to row locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库命令，用来查看一条查询实际会怎样执行（用没用索引、扫了多少行）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: EXPLAIN is a database command that shows how a query will actually execute, including whether it uses an index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制查询返回的最大行数，减少不必要的数据传输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LIMIT caps the number of rows a query returns, cutting unnecessary data transfer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 合并多条查询结果的 SQL 关键字，有时比一条 OR 查询更利于走索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UNION combines the results of multiple queries and can sometimes use indexes more effectively than a single OR query.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门做全文搜索和复杂查询的搜索引擎。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a search engine specialized in full-text search and complex queries.

optionExplanations: 直接引入 Elasticsearch 能解决问题，但要多背一整套集群运维，只在一开始就确定要走这条路时才划算。
给常用搜索列建索引、用 EXPLAIN/避免 SELECT */LIMIT/UNION 替代 OR 优化查询，不引入新组件就能省掉一整套集群运维。
把存储方案整体换成 NoSQL 解决不了查询模式本身的问题，索引和过滤逻辑还是要重新设计。
把过滤逻辑放到前端做，意味着全量数据仍要传到客户端，延迟反而更差。
optionExplanations_en: Bringing in Elasticsearch directly solves it but adds a whole cluster to operate — only worth it if that path is already decided.
Indexing common search columns and optimizing the query — EXPLAIN, avoiding SELECT *, LIMIT, UNION instead of OR — skips a new component entirely.
Swapping storage for NoSQL wholesale doesn't fix the query pattern itself; indexing and filtering still need redesigning.
Pushing filtering to the frontend means the full dataset still reaches the client — latency gets worse, not better.

scenario: 票务库查询模式很杂（关键词、日期、城市、类型），有人提议给每个字段都建索引。
scenario_en: Ticket queries hit many columns — keyword, date, city, category — and someone suggests indexing every one of them.
q: 给表加大量索引的代价是？
q_en: What is the cost of adding many indexes to the table?
options: 读取会变得更慢
数据库从此无法备份
存储增加、写入变慢，且仍拿部分匹配没办法
索引会定期自动过期失效，需要重建整个集群
why: 索引是拿写性能和存储换读性能；普通索引也救不了部分字符串匹配。票务系统查询模式多样，索引数量要权衡。
why_en: Indexes trade extra storage and slower writes for faster reads, and standard indexes still cannot help partial-string matches like searching just 'Taylor'.
options_en: Reads will get slower.
The database can no longer be backed up.
Storage grows, writes slow down, and partial matches are still weak.
Indexes periodically expire on their own and the whole cluster must be rebuilt.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次插入或更新数据时，数据库都要同步更新相关索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Every insert or update must also update the related index structures, adding write overhead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只输入词语的一部分（如 'Taylor'）也要能搜到完整结果，普通索引对这种查询帮助有限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partial string matching means a search like 'Taylor' should still find 'Taylor Swift', which standard indexes handle poorly.

optionExplanations: 索引恰恰是为了让读更快，把代价说成读变慢是反了。
备份策略不受索引数量影响，两者没有关联。
每次插入/更新都要同步维护索引，占用更多存储、拖慢写入，而且普通索引还是救不了部分字符串匹配。
索引不存在定期过期或需要重建整个集群这种机制，这个说法凭空捏造了代价。
optionExplanations_en: Indexes exist specifically to make reads faster — claiming they slow reads down gets it backwards.
Backup strategy isn't affected by the number of indexes — the two are unrelated.
Every insert/update has to maintain the index too, adding storage and slowing writes, and plain indexes still can't help partial matching.
Indexes don't periodically expire or require rebuilding a whole cluster — this claims a cost that doesn't exist.

scenario: 活动名要支持关键词搜索，但团队暂时不想再养一套独立搜索引擎。
scenario_en: Event names need keyword search, but the team would rather not run a separate search engine yet.
q: 关于数据库内建全文搜索，正确的是？
q_en: What is true about built-in database full-text search?
options: 全文搜索只有 Elasticsearch 才能做到
Postgres 的全文搜索底层其实就是 Lucene 引擎
MySQL 完全没有内建的全文索引功能
PG 和 MySQL 各有内建全文索引，都不基于 Lucene
why: PG 的 tsvector+GIN 和 MySQL 全文索引都是数据库自研实现，查询关键词比 LIKE 全表扫描快得多；Lucene 是独立搜索引擎的技术，不是数据库自带的。
why_en: PostgreSQL's tsvector-plus-GIN and MySQL's own full-text index are both native database features, and neither one uses Lucene, which is what powers Elasticsearch.
options_en: Only Elasticsearch is capable of doing full-text search at all.
Postgres's full-text search is really just the Lucene engine under the hood.
MySQL has no built-in full-text indexing feature whatsoever.
Postgres and MySQL each ship their own built-in full-text index, neither one based on Lucene.

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 把文本预处理成的可搜索词形式，是全文搜索的基础结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tsvector is PostgreSQL's preprocessed, searchable representation of text used for full-text search.

termDefinitions.meaning: PostgreSQL 上适合给 tsvector 这类多值列建的索引类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GIN index is a PostgreSQL index type well suited to multi-value columns like tsvector.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 底层使用的全文搜索库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lucene is the full-text search library that powers Elasticsearch under the hood.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于倒排索引的独立搜索引擎，常用于全文搜索场景。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a standalone search engine built on inverted indexes, commonly used for full-text search.

optionExplanations: 低估了数据库自带的全文能力，PG 和 MySQL 都有自己的内建实现。
把 Lucene 这个独立搜索引擎的技术错按到了 Postgres 头上，PG 的全文搜索是自研的 tsvector+GIN。
MySQL 其实早就有自己的全文索引功能，这个说法与事实相反。
两边各自都有一套自己写的全文检索，谁也没借用那套独立搜索引擎的技术，速度都甩开逐行比对一大截。
optionExplanations_en: This underestimates what databases already have built in — both PG and MySQL ship their own full-text implementations.
This misattributes Lucene, a separate search engine's technology, to Postgres — PG's full-text search is its own tsvector+GIN.
MySQL has actually had its own full-text indexing for a long time — this claim is the opposite of true.
Each database ships its own home-grown full-text engine, neither borrowed from that separate search-engine project, and both leave row-by-row scanning far behind.

scenario: 准备在 PostgreSQL 上启用全文索引，先要说清它拿什么换了关键词查询能力。
scenario_en: You're about to turn on full-text indexing in PostgreSQL, so first name what it trades away for keyword search.
q: 数据库全文索引的代价是？
q_en: What is the cost of database full-text indexes?
options: 多占存储、查询更慢，还要特殊维护
会导致数据永久丢失
和数据库的事务处理机制完全不兼容
只支持英文这一种语言
why: 全文索引占更多存储、有时查询比标准索引慢，还需要特殊查询语法和维护方式——功能换来了额外复杂度。
why_en: Full-text indexes need extra storage, can sometimes be slower to query than standard indexes, and require special query syntax and upkeep.
options_en: It needs extra storage, queries can be slower than plain indexes, and it needs special syntax and upkeep.
It can cause data loss.
It is incompatible with the database's transaction processing mechanism.
It only supports English.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门为文本关键词查询优化的数据库索引类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full-text index is a database index type optimized for keyword text search.

optionExplanations: 占更多存储空间，有时比标准索引慢，查询语法和维护方式都要特殊处理。
全文索引不会导致数据丢失，这个代价是凭空捏造的。
全文索引照常参与事务，跟数据库事务处理机制没有不兼容的问题。
多数全文搜索方案都支持多语言配置，只支持英文不是它的主要限制。
optionExplanations_en: It takes more storage, is sometimes slower than a standard index, and needs special query syntax and upkeep.
A full-text index doesn't cause permanent data loss — that cost is invented.
A full-text index still participates in transactions normally — there's no incompatibility with the DB's transaction mechanism.
Most full-text search setups support multiple languages — English-only isn't its real limitation.

scenario: 搜索要支持关键词部分匹配、错别字容忍（'Tayler Swift' 也要搜到 Taylor Swift）、复杂查询和高流量。
scenario_en: Search must support partial keywords, typos like 'Tayler Swift', complex queries, and high traffic.
q: Great 级选型是？
q_en: What is the Great-level search choice?
options: 在现有表上再多加几个 B-tree 索引就能解决问题
把全部数据一股脑塞进 Redis 里存着
引入 Elasticsearch，靠倒排索引+模糊搜索
让客户端下载全量数据到本地自己搜索
why: Elasticsearch 靠倒排索引直接定位含关键词的记录，模糊搜索还能容忍拼写错误，这两点纯 SQL 都很难做到。
why_en: Elasticsearch locates matching documents directly through its inverted index and adds fuzzy search for typo tolerance, both of which plain SQL struggles to match.
whenOtherWins: 查询模式简单（精确/前缀为主）且规模可控时，Postgres 自带的 tsvector+GIN 更省一套集群运维。
tradeoff: 全文检索能力与容错 vs 多养一套 Elasticsearch 集群
options_en: Just add a few more B-tree indexes on the existing table and that would solve it.
Cram the entire dataset into Redis and store it there instead.
Adopt Elasticsearch, which relies on an inverted index plus fuzzy search.
Have the client download the entire dataset and search it locally on-device.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个词映射到包含它的文档列表的索引结构，是搜索引擎快速检索的基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each word to the list of documents containing it, which is what makes search engines fast.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许查询词和结果之间有少量拼写差异（编辑距离）也能匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fuzzy search allows a small number of spelling differences, or edit distance, between the query and the match.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于倒排索引的分布式搜索引擎，擅长全文搜索和复杂查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a distributed search engine built on inverted indexes, strong at full-text search and complex queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库默认的排序型索引，适合等值和前缀匹配，不擅长部分匹配或容错。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree index is a database's default sorted index, good for equality and prefix lookups but weak at partial matches or typo tolerance.

optionExplanations: 在现有表上再多几个 B-tree 索引依然搞不定部分匹配和错别字容忍，方向没对上需求。
Redis 没有内建的全文/模糊检索能力，把数据塞进去也搜不出容错结果。
换一套专门做检索的系统，靠反查词表直接跳到含关键词的记录，还顺带能容错拼写，只是要多养一套集群。
全量数据下载到客户端既慢又不现实，规模一大根本传不完。
optionExplanations_en: More B-tree indexes on the existing table still can't handle partial matching or typo tolerance — it doesn't address what's actually needed.
Redis has no built-in full-text or fuzzy search capability — dumping data in there won't produce tolerant matches.
Bring in a system built for search: it jumps straight to matching records via a reverse word lookup and tolerates typos too, at the cost of running an extra cluster.
Downloading the full dataset to the client is slow and unrealistic — it won't finish transferring at scale.

scenario: 活动表百万行，按关键词搜索的 LIKE '%taylor%' 已经慢到秒级。
scenario_en: The events table has millions of rows and a LIKE '%taylor%' keyword search already takes seconds.
q: 在「关键词如何定位记录」这个维度上，倒排索引与 LIKE 全表扫描的区别是？
q_en: On keyword lookup, how does an inverted index differ from a LIKE full table scan?
options: 两者都必须逐行扫描全表
LIKE 更快，因为它直接在数据库引擎内部执行
倒排索引只能匹配整句，不能拆词
倒排索引按词直接命中文档；LIKE 要逐行扫描
why: 倒排索引把查询从「扫每行找词」倒过来变成「按词查文档清单」，这正是 Elasticsearch 高效检索的根基。
why_en: An inverted index flips the search from scanning every row for a word to looking up the word's document list directly, which is why Elasticsearch is fast.
tradeoff: 倒排索引按词直接命中 vs LIKE 前导通配符逐行扫描
options_en: Both approaches must scan every row of the table.
LIKE is faster because it runs directly inside the database engine.
An inverted index can only match a whole sentence, not individual words.
An inverted index maps each word straight to its documents; LIKE has to scan row by row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个词映射到包含它的文档列表的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each word to the list of documents that contain it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库对 LIKE '%词%' 这类前导通配符查询逐行检查整张表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A LIKE full table scan checks every row of a table one by one when the pattern has a leading wildcard.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖排序结构查找的普通索引，对前导通配符查询无能为力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree index relies on sorted order for lookups and cannot help with a leading-wildcard query.

optionExplanations: 把两种机制的查找方式说成一样，忽略了倒排索引按词查文档清单的优势。
执行位置不是这里的决定性因素，LIKE 该扫描的行数并不会因为在数据库内执行而减少。
误解了倒排索引只支持整句匹配——它其实是按词分词后建的索引。
查找方向反过来了：不是把每行都看一遍找词，而是拿词直接查到它出现在哪些文档里；LIKE 依旧得一行行核对。
optionExplanations_en: Claiming both work the same way ignores the inverted index's advantage of looking up documents by word directly.
Where it executes isn't the deciding factor — LIKE still scans the same number of rows regardless of running inside the database.
This misunderstands the inverted index as only matching whole phrases — it's actually built by tokenizing into words.
The lookup direction flips: instead of scanning every row for the word, it looks the word up and gets back exactly which documents contain it, while LIKE still checks row by row.

scenario: 主库仍是 PostgreSQL、搜索走 Elasticsearch，两边不能长时间不一致。
scenario_en: PostgreSQL stays the source of truth while search runs on Elasticsearch, and the two cannot drift for long.
q: 如何保证 Elasticsearch 索引与 PostgreSQL 数据同步？
q_en: How do you keep the Elasticsearch index synced with PostgreSQL?
options: 双写：应用在一次请求里同时写 PG 和 ES 两边
用 CDC 捕获 PG 变更，近实时同步到 ES
每天定时全量重建一次索引
让 ES 直接读 PG 的底层表文件
why: CDC 监听 PG 的变更流并回放到 ES，让搜索索引近实时跟随主库；这是保持两个存储一致的标准机制。
why_en: Change data capture streams Postgres inserts, updates, and deletes into the Elasticsearch index for near-real-time synchronization.
diagram:
graph LR
    PG[(Postgres source)] --> CDC[CDC or outbox]
    CDC --> Worker[Index worker]
    Worker --> ES[(Elasticsearch)]
    Search[Search Service] --> ES
options_en: Dual-write: within one request the application writes to both Postgres and Elasticsearch itself.
Use CDC to capture Postgres changes and sync them to Elasticsearch near-real-time.
Fully rebuild the entire index once a day on a fixed schedule.
Have Elasticsearch read Postgres's underlying table files directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获数据库变更（增/删/改）并把它们实时或近实时地传播给下游系统的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CDC, or Change Data Capture, captures database inserts, updates, and deletes and streams them to downstream systems in near real time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用代码同时写两个存储，容易因部分失败导致两边数据不一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dual write means the application writes to two stores at once, which risks inconsistency if one write fails.

optionExplanations: 应用在一次请求里同时负责两次写入，任一次失败就会导致两边不一致，风险都压在应用层。
订阅主库的变更事件、把它们搬到搜索那边重放，两边数据就能几乎同步，应用代码完全不用改。
每天全量重建期间数据是陈旧的，而且重建成本很高，不适合抢票这种高频变化场景。
ES 不支持也不该直接解析数据库文件，这条路径在架构上根本不存在。
optionExplanations_en: The application handles both writes within one request — any single failure leaves the two stores out of sync, with all the risk in application code.
Subscribe to the primary store's change events and replay them into the search side, keeping the two nearly in sync without touching a line of application code.
A daily full rebuild leaves data stale in between and is costly — a poor fit for a fast-changing ticket-rush scenario.
ES neither supports nor should directly parse database files — this path doesn't architecturally exist.

scenario: 用户常把 Taylor 打成 Tayler，搜不到结果就直接离开，不会再改拼写。
scenario_en: Users type Tayler instead of Taylor, get nothing back, and leave rather than retry the spelling.
q: 模糊搜索（fuzzy search）解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem does fuzzy search solve?
options: 容忍拼写错误和输入变体写法，比如 Tayler 也能匹配到 Taylor
只是让原本就已经能精确匹配上的那些查询，响应速度进一步变得更快一点而已
自动把搜索出来的所有结果内容，翻译成好几种不同的语言版本
只是想办法把索引本身占用的存储体积，压缩得更加小巧紧凑一点
why: 用户输入常有错别字；模糊搜索按编辑距离容错，把近似拼写映射到正确结果，这一点纯 SQL 很难做到。
why_en: Fuzzy search tolerates typos by allowing a small edit distance, matching something like Tayler Swift to Taylor Swift, which plain SQL struggles to do.
options_en: It tolerates typos and spelling variants, like matching Tayler to Taylor.
It just makes those queries that were already exact matches respond a little faster, nothing more.
It automatically translates the search results' content into several different languages.
It's really just about shrinking the storage footprint of the index itself down further.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许查询词和匹配结果之间存在少量字符差异（编辑距离）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fuzzy search allows a small number of character differences, or edit distance, between the query and the match.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个字符串变成另一个字符串所需的最少增删改次数，用来衡量拼写相似度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Edit distance is the minimum number of insertions, deletions, or substitutions needed to turn one string into another, used to measure spelling similarity.

optionExplanations: 打字总会手滑，这套机制按字符差异容忍误差，把敲错的词照样指向该指向的结果。
精确匹配速度不是模糊搜索要解决的问题，把两者的目标搞混了。
模糊搜索不涉及语言翻译，跟多语言支持是两回事。
索引体积压缩不是模糊搜索的目标，容错才是它存在的意义。
optionExplanations_en: Typos happen constantly, and this mechanism tolerates the character-level difference, still pointing a misspelled word at the result it meant to hit.
Fuzzy search isn't about speeding up exact matches — that conflates two different goals.
Fuzzy search has nothing to do with language translation, a completely separate concern.
Shrinking index size isn't fuzzy search's goal — tolerance for typos is the whole point of it.

scenario: 决定引入 Elasticsearch 之前，面试里要主动把它的代价说出来。
scenario_en: Before committing to Elasticsearch, you want to name its costs out loud in the interview.
q: 引入 Elasticsearch 的真实代价有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What real costs come with introducing Elasticsearch?
options: 同步 ES 索引与 PostgreSQL 很复杂，需要可靠一致性机制
维护 ES 集群带来额外基础设施复杂度和成本
倒排索引不支持全文搜索
ES 无法横向扩展
why: 两大代价：同步链路（CDC）要保证数据一致不丢不重；多养一套集群带来运维和成本。后两个选项与事实相反。
why_en: Elasticsearch costs a synchronization pipeline that must stay consistent with Postgres, plus the added infrastructure and cost of running another cluster.
options_en: Keeping the ES index in sync with Postgres is complex and needs a reliable consistency mechanism.
Running an ES cluster adds extra infrastructure complexity and cost.
Inverted indexes do not support full-text search.
Elasticsearch cannot scale horizontally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据库变更实时或近实时同步到下游系统的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CDC streams database changes to downstream systems in real time or near real time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把词映射到文档列表的索引结构，是全文搜索的实现基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps words to document lists and underlies full-text search.

optionExplanations: 数据一变就要保证 ES 不丢不重地跟上，同步链路本身要处理故障重试和顺序保证。
多养一套独立集群，需要专门团队做容量规划、版本升级和监控。
把倒排索引的核心用途说反了——它正是全文搜索的实现基础，不是不支持。
把 ES 的横向扩展能力说反了——它天生支持分片，横向扩展恰恰是它的优势。
optionExplanations_en: Every data change has to reach ES without loss or duplication — the sync pipeline itself has to handle retries and ordering.
Running a separate cluster needs a dedicated team for capacity planning, version upgrades, and monitoring.
This reverses the inverted index's core purpose — it's literally the foundation of full-text search, not something it lacks.
This reverses ES's scaling story — it natively shards and horizontal scaling is actually one of its strengths.

scenario: 同样的热门搜索词（如 'Taylor Swift'）被海量用户反复查询，想减轻搜索引擎和数据库的负载。
scenario_en: The same popular search term, such as 'Taylor Swift', is repeated by many users, and you want to reduce load on search and the database.
q: 该采用什么缓存方案？
q_en: What caching approach should search use?
options: 直接禁止用户重复搜索
每次都查 ES，保证绝对新鲜
把结果存进客户端 localStorage
用 Redis 缓存查询结果 + TTL
why: 以查询参数拼 key 唯一标识一次查询，结果存进 Redis/Memcached，设 TTL 控制陈旧度，重复查询直接命中而不打后端。
why_en: Build the cache key from the query parameters, store the result in Redis or Memcached, and set a TTL so repeated searches hit the cache instead of the backend.
whenOtherWins: 若搜索结果因人而异（个性化），无法共享缓存条目，这套查询缓存就不适用。
tradeoff: 共享查询结果缓存 vs 每次都查最新数据
options_en: Simply forbid repeated searches.
Query Elasticsearch every time to guarantee freshness.
Store results in the client's localStorage.
Cache query results in Redis with a TTL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，过期后必须重新查询并回填。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cache entry stays valid before it must be refetched and refilled.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用查询参数拼出的唯一标识，相同参数命中同一条缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache key is a unique identifier built from the query parameters so identical queries hit the same cached entry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的外部内存缓存服务，供多个应用实例共享结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis and Memcached are common external in-memory cache services shared across application instances.

optionExplanations: 禁止用户重复搜索会损害体验，也没有真正解决重复计算的问题。
每次都查 ES 能保证最新结果，但热门词依旧反复打满搜索引擎和数据库，只在负载压力不大时才划算。
存进客户端 localStorage 是单用户私有存储，换个用户就没有缓存效果，命中率低。
把请求参数拼成一个键，算出来的结果存进共享的内存存储并挂个过期时间，下一个问同样问题的人直接拿现成的。
optionExplanations_en: Blocking repeat searches hurts the experience and doesn't actually solve the redundant-computation problem.
Querying ES every time guarantees freshness, but hot terms still hammer the backend repeatedly — only worth it when load is low.
Storing results in client localStorage is private per user — a different user gets no cache benefit, so hit rate is low.
Turn the request parameters into a single key, park the computed result in a shared in-memory store with an expiry, and the next identical ask just grabs it ready-made.

scenario: 热门搜索词被大量用户反复查询，你要为搜索结果设计一条缓存记录。
scenario_en: A popular search term is queried repeatedly, and you need one cache record for the search result.
q: 补全搜索缓存条目的设计：
q_en: Fill in the search-cache entry design.
text: 缓存 key 由{{查询参数}}构造（如 search:keyword=Taylor Swift&start=2021-01-01&end=2021-12-31），value 是匹配的活动列表，示例 TTL 设为 {{24}} 小时。
why: key 必须唯一标识一组查询条件才能正确命中缓存；示例 TTL 是 60*60*24 秒＝24 小时，按新鲜度需求调整。
why_en: The cache key is built from the search parameters and the example entry uses a twenty-four-hour TTL.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，超过这个时长条目会过期失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the length of time a cache entry stays valid before it expires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于唯一标识一次查询的字符串，通常由查询参数拼接而成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache key is a string that uniquely identifies a query, typically built by concatenating the query parameters.

scenario: 搜索结果缓存命中率很高，但只要有新活动上架，旧结果立刻就是错的。
scenario_en: The search-result cache hits often, but the moment a new event goes on sale the cached results are wrong.
q: 搜索结果缓存的主要挑战是？
q_en: What is the main challenge with caching search results?
options: Redis 装不下字符串类型的 key
失效管理难，陈旧缓存会返回错误结果
缓存反而会拖慢搜索速度
TTL 这个参数根本设不了
why: 查询与结果没有直接映射，数据一变很难精确失效；用 TTL + cache tags 组合失效，同时防未命中风暴。
why_en: Cache invalidation is hard because queries and results have no direct mapping, so combine TTLs with cache-tag triggers and watch for miss storms at peak load.
options_en: Redis cannot store string-type keys.
Invalidation is hard — stale entries can serve wrong results.
Caching actually slows search down.
TTL simply cannot be configured.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据变化后主动使相关缓存条目过期或删除，避免返回陈旧结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache invalidation expires or removes cache entries when the underlying data changes so stale results are not served.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给缓存条目打标签，数据变化时可以按标签批量失效相关条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache tags label cache entries so a batch of related entries can be invalidated together when data changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量缓存同时失效或过期，瞬间涌入后端的请求压垮系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A miss storm happens when many cache entries expire at once and the resulting flood of requests overwhelms the backend.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许拼写差异的搜索方式，会让结果集合更难与固定 key 对应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fuzzy search tolerates spelling differences, which makes its result sets harder to map to a fixed cache key.

optionExplanations: Redis 原生支持字符串类型的 key，这不是它的限制。
查询和结果之间没有直接映射，数据一变很难精确知道该失效哪些查询缓存，模糊搜索更复杂，陈旧缓存会返回错误结果。
缓存命中恰恰是用来加速重复查询的，把作用方向说反了。
TTL 是缓存的基础参数，一直都能设置，这个限制不存在。
optionExplanations_en: Redis natively supports string keys — that's not a limitation here.
There's no direct mapping from query to result, so a data change makes it hard to know precisely which cached queries to invalidate — stale entries return wrong results.
A cache hit exists specifically to speed up repeat queries — this states the effect backwards.
TTL is a basic cache parameter that's always settable — this limitation doesn't exist.

scenario: 搜索 QPS 很高但查询重复度大，团队在犹豫要不要在 ES 前面再自建一层缓存。
scenario_en: Search QPS is high and queries repeat a lot, so the team debates adding its own cache in front of Elasticsearch.
q: Elasticsearch 自带哪些缓存能力？
q_en: What caching capabilities does Elasticsearch provide by default?
options: node 级过滤缓存 + 分片级响应缓存，两层内建
完全只依赖客户端浏览器自己那一份本地缓存内容，别无其它
ES 从头到尾都完完全全不做任何形式的查询结果缓存处理
只缓存写请求这一侧的相关数据内容，从来都不缓存查询的结果
why: ES 内建两层缓存：node 级的 query cache 缓存 filter 结果，分片级的 request cache 缓存完整响应，无需自建缓存层就能降低重复查询开销。
why_en: Elasticsearch keeps a node-level query cache for filter results and a shard-level request cache for full responses, cutting repeat-query cost without a separate cache layer.
options_en: Two built-in layers: a node-level filter cache and a shard-level response cache.
It relies entirely on nothing but the client browser's own local cache, and nothing else.
Elasticsearch, from end to end, does absolutely no caching of query results whatsoever.
It only caches the write-request side of things, and never caches query results at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: Elasticsearch 把一个索引切分成的更小单元，便于分布式存储和并行查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shard is a smaller unit Elasticsearch splits an index into, enabling distributed storage and parallel querying.

termDefinitions.meaning: node 级缓存，专门保存过滤（filter）条件的结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query cache is a node-level cache that stores the results of filter clauses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片级缓存，保存完整搜索响应，对聚合类查询效果明显。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The request cache is a shard-level cache that stores full search responses, which helps a lot for aggregation-heavy queries.

optionExplanations: 搜索引擎自己就留了两道缓存：node 级的一道管过滤后的候选集，分片级的一道管拼好的整份响应，聚合查询尤其受益。
把缓存责任完全推给客户端，客户端缓存没法被其他用户共享，命中率低。
与事实相反，ES 内建两层分片缓存，不是完全不做缓存。
把缓存和写路径搞反了——查询恰恰是最需要缓存的路径，ES 不缓存写请求。
optionExplanations_en: The search engine keeps two cache layers on its own — a node-level one for the filtered candidate set and a shard-level one for the assembled response — and aggregations benefit the most.
This pushes caching entirely to the client, but client-side caches can't be shared across users, so hit rate stays low.
This is the opposite of true — ES has two built-in shard-level caches, not zero caching.
This reverses cache and write path — reads benefit most from caching; ES doesn't cache writes.

scenario: 搜索结果不做个性化（同一查询对所有用户返回相同结果），想让全球用户的重复查询延迟更低。
scenario_en: Search results are not personalized, so the same query returns the same results for every user worldwide.
q: 还可以再加哪一层缓存？
q_en: What extra cache layer can you add?
options: 给每个用户配专属服务器
在每个国家部署一套 ES
用 CDN 就近缓存搜索结果
取消搜索缓存
why: 结果对所有用户一致是前提；CDN 把搜索结果缓存到离用户近的边缘节点，重复查询就近返回，全球延迟更低。
why_en: As long as results are not personalized, a CDN like CloudFront can cache them at edge nodes near users so repeated queries return faster worldwide.
whenOtherWins: 一旦搜索结果个性化（因人而异），CDN 共享缓存就不适用，只能退回服务端/用户级缓存。
tradeoff: 全球边缘就近命中 vs 结果必须对所有用户一致
options_en: Give every user a dedicated server.
Deploy a full Elasticsearch cluster in every country.
Use a CDN, like CloudFront, to cache results near each query.
Remove search caching altogether.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘节点上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN, or content delivery network, caches content on edge servers close to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一查询对不同用户返回不同结果，这类结果无法被共享缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Personalized results mean the same query returns different results per user, which a shared cache cannot serve.

optionExplanations: 给每个用户配专属服务器成本不现实，也没有解决地理延迟这个真正问题。
在每个国家部署一套独立 ES 会带来数据同步和一致性的新问题，比要解决的问题更麻烦。
同一查询人人同解，就能囤在离用户最近的边缘；省下的回源量 ≈ 重复查询占比 × 边缘覆盖率。
取消搜索缓存会退回每次都打搜索后端，负载和延迟都变差，跟目标背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Dedicating a server per user isn't cost-realistic and doesn't solve the actual geographic-latency problem.
Deploying a separate ES cluster per country introduces new data-sync and consistency problems, worse than the one being solved.
When the same query gives everyone the same answer it can sit on the nearest edge; origin traffic saved is roughly the repeat-query share times edge coverage.
Removing the search cache falls back to hitting the backend every time, making load and latency worse — the opposite of the goal.

scenario: 把搜索结果缓存到 CDN 边缘后，新活动一上架就要决定该失效哪些边缘条目。
scenario_en: Once search results sit on CDN edges, a newly listed event forces you to decide which edge entries to invalidate.
q: CDN/自适应缓存搜索结果的一致性难点在哪？
q_en: Where is the consistency problem in CDN or adaptive caching for search results?
options: CDN 边缘节点数量太少
查询串和结果之间没有直接映射，难精确失效
CDN 边缘节点天生不支持 HTTPS
缓存后搜索结果顺序会打乱
why: 同一个新活动可能影响无数种查询的结果，而缓存 key 只是查询串——找不到该失效哪些 key 的精确映射，这是一致性的本质难题。
why_en: A single data change can affect countless possible queries, but the cache key is just a query string, so there is no precise mapping telling you which keys to invalidate.
options_en: There are too few CDN edge nodes.
Query strings have no direct mapping to the results they affect, so precise invalidation is hard.
CDN edge nodes inherently do not support HTTPS.
Caching scrambles the order of search results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统自动学习并缓存最高频查询的策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Adaptive caching automatically learns and caches the most frequently requested queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从「数据变化」到「该失效哪些缓存 key」之间的对应关系；查询缓存里这层映射通常不存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Invalidation mapping is the link from a data change to the cache keys it affects, which query-result caches typically lack.

optionExplanations: 节点数量不是这里的核心问题，跟一致性难点没有直接关系。
一条新活动能牵动成千上万种不同的查询组合，但缓存记的只是查询本身，根本反推不出该清哪些条目。
CDN 边缘节点早已普遍支持 HTTPS，这不是限制它的因素。
缓存不会改变结果内部的排序逻辑，跟排序打乱没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Node count isn't the core issue here — it has no direct bearing on the consistency problem.
One new event can ripple into countless different query combinations, but the cache only remembers the query string, so there's no way to trace which entries to clear.
CDN edge nodes have long supported HTTPS broadly — that's not a limiting factor.
Caching doesn't change the internal ordering of results — it's unrelated to any ordering issue.

scenario: 面试收尾要归纳这题的可迁移模式，而 Ticketmaster 本身没有按地理位置检索的需求。
scenario_en: You wrap up by naming the transferable patterns, noting Ticketmaster never needs location-based lookup.
q: Ticketmaster 这题主要体现了哪些系统设计模式？（多选）
q_en: Which system-design patterns does the Ticketmaster problem mainly show?
options: 处理竞争（Dealing with Contention）——高并发抢同一张票
读扩展（Scaling Reads）——开售时活动页被打爆
实时更新（Real-time Updates）——座位图与队列排位推送
地理空间索引（Geospatial Index）
why: 三个可迁移的模式：竞争处理（防双订）、读扩展（缓存+横向扩展）、实时更新（SSE/WebSocket）。地理索引是 Uber/Yelp 类题的模式，本题没用到。
why_en: This problem showcases dealing with contention, scaling reads, and real-time updates, while geospatial indexing belongs to problems like Uber or Yelp instead.
options_en: Dealing with Contention — many users racing for the same ticket.
Scaling Reads — event pages get hammered when tickets go on sale.
Real-time Updates — seat map and queue position pushed live.
Geospatial Index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个请求同时抢占同一资源时如何保证正确性的设计模式（如防止双重下单）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dealing with Contention is the design pattern for keeping correctness when many requests race for the same resource, such as preventing double booking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读流量远大于写流量时，用缓存和横向扩展来支撑高并发读取的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scaling Reads is the pattern of using caching and horizontal scaling to support very high read traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器主动把状态变化推送给客户端的模式，如 SSE 或 WebSocket。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Real-time Updates is the pattern of pushing state changes from server to client live, using mechanisms like SSE or WebSocket.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按地理位置快速检索附近结果的索引结构，常见于打车、点评类应用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A geospatial index is a structure for quickly finding nearby results by location, common in ride-hailing or review apps.

optionExplanations: 对应票务的防双订设计：数据库事务、OCC、Redis 分布式锁都在处理同一资源被高并发抢占的问题。
对应活动页缓存 + 横向扩展设计：读远多于写时靠这两招把读压力扛住。
对应 SSE/WebSocket 推送座位状态和排队进度，让客户端不用刷新就能看到最新变化。
本题不涉及「附近的活动」这类按地理位置检索的需求，地理空间索引没有用到。
optionExplanations_en: This maps to the anti-double-booking design: transactions, OCC, and Redis's distributed lock all handle contention over one resource.
This maps to the event-page cache plus horizontal scaling design: when reads vastly outnumber writes, these two techniques absorb the pressure.
This maps to SSE/WebSocket pushing seat status and queue position so clients see updates without refreshing.
This problem never needs "events near me" style geographic lookup, so geospatial indexing isn't used.

scenario: Ticketmaster 这类产品题只有 45 分钟，功能需求和非功能需求都已列好，接下来要决定动手推进的顺序。
scenario_en: A product-style Ticketmaster question gives you 45 minutes; the functional and non-functional requirements are listed, and you must pick the order of attack.
q: Ticketmaster 动手设计时，推进顺序该怎么定？
q_en: In what order should you build out the Ticketmaster design?
options: 先逐条满足功能需求搭出可跑的高层设计，再用非功能需求驱动后续 deep dive 的顺序
一上来就把分布式锁、Elasticsearch、缓存这些 deep dive 全部设计透，最后再回头拼高层架构图
功能与非功能需求混着来，想到哪画到哪，哪块自己最熟就先深挖哪块
先照可用性、低延迟这些非功能需求搭出骨架，把功能需求留到最后收尾再补上
options_en: First satisfy the functional requirements one by one into a working high-level design, then let the non-functional requirements drive the order of the deep dives.
Design all the deep dives — distributed lock, Elasticsearch, caching — fully up front, and only stitch the high-level architecture together at the end.
Mix functional and non-functional requirements, sketch whatever comes to mind, and deep-dive whichever part you know best first.
Build the skeleton from non-functional requirements like availability and low latency first, and leave the functional requirements for the very end.
why: 功能需求逐条搭起高层设计能先跑通主路径不迷失，非功能需求再指出该往哪深挖；代价是早期只上抽象组件，深度推迟到 deep dive。
why_en: Building the high-level design functional-requirement by functional-requirement gets the main path working without getting lost, then the non-functional ones point you to where to go deep; the cost is early components stay abstract until the deep dives.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官开场就明说只想聊某个 deep dive（如只考防双订），可以跳过完整高层设计，直接进那一个点。
tradeoff: 聚焦推进主路径 vs 提前深挖单点

termDefinitions.meaning: 在高层设计之上对某个非功能需求做的深入设计段落，如防双订、读扩展、搜索优化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is a focused design segment that goes deep on one non-functional requirement on top of the high-level design, such as no-double-booking or scaling reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用「系统应当……」描述系统质量的需求，如可用性、延迟、一致性，用来驱动 deep dive 的选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements describe system qualities in "the system should..." terms — availability, latency, consistency — and drive which deep dives to pick.

optionExplanations: 顺着功能需求一条条搭，主路径先能跑通；再让可用性、延迟等质量目标指出下一步该深挖哪里。
没有高层骨架就钻细节，容易做得又深又散、时间失控——只有面试官指定只聊某个点时才合适。
无序穿插会让设计凌乱、面试官难跟，还容易偏向你的舒适区而漏掉核心功能。
骨架先照质量目标搭，会架空还没定义的主路径，功能没落地时深挖也无处附着。
optionExplanations_en: Building along the functional requirements gets the main path working first, then quality goals like availability and latency point to the next deep dive.
Diving into details with no skeleton tends to go deep but scattered and blows the clock — only fits when the interviewer picks one topic.
Interleaving with no order makes the design messy and hard to follow, and drifts toward your comfort zone while core features slip.
A skeleton built from quality goals floats above an undefined main path, leaving deep dives nothing to attach to before features land.

scenario: 缓存和无状态 Event Service 横向扩展都上了，但缓存未命中时所有实例的读请求最终都落在同一个 Postgres 主库上。
scenario_en: Caching and horizontal scaling of the stateless Event Service are in place, but on a cache miss every instance ends up reading from the same Postgres primary.
q: 应用层已扩，数据库读还是瓶颈，怎么继续扩读？
q_en: App tier scaled but the DB read path is still the bottleneck — how do you scale reads further?
options: 继续堆更多无状态 Event Service 实例，实例越多整体读吞吐就越高
把 Postgres 纵向扩展成更大的单机，用硬件把读压力顶回去、回避分布式复杂度
加只读副本分摊读流量，再按 eventId 把数据切成多个分片拆开数据量与写压力
给每个 Event Service 实例挂一个本地内存缓存，让它彻底不再回主库
options_en: Keep adding more stateless Event Service instances — more instances means higher overall read throughput.
Vertically scale Postgres onto one bigger machine, throwing hardware at the read load to avoid distributed complexity.
Add read replicas to spread read traffic, then shard the data by eventId to split data volume and write load.
Give each Event Service instance a local in-memory cache so it never goes back to the primary.
why: 无状态实例共享同一主库，读风暴最终都压回 Postgres；只读副本把读扇出到多个节点，分片按 eventId 拆数据与写。代价：副本有复制延迟、分片让跨片查询和再平衡变复杂。
why_en: Stateless instances share one primary, so the read storm lands back on Postgres; read replicas fan reads out across nodes and sharding by eventId splits data and writes. The cost is replica lag plus harder cross-shard queries and rebalancing.
whenOtherWins: 若缓存命中率已经极高、未命中的读量本就很小，单主库配几个只读副本就够，不必背上分片的运维负担。
tradeoff: 数据库读吞吐 vs 复制延迟与分片运维复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: replication 复制出的只读数据库节点，把读请求从主库扇出分摊，代价是数据有短暂复制延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only database node produced by replication that fans reads off the primary, at the cost of brief replication lag.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片：按某个键（如 eventId）把数据水平切成多份分别存放，拆开单库的数据量与写压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding horizontally splits data by a key such as eventId into separate partitions, dividing a single database data volume and write load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复制：把主库的数据同步到一或多个副本节点，用于分摊读或做高可用，副本会有复制延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication copies a primary data to one or more replica nodes to spread reads or provide high availability, with some replication lag.

optionExplanations: 再多无状态实例也共享同一主库，缓存未命中时读风暴仍砸向那一个 Postgres，连接被打满。
纵向扩展有物理上限、还是单点，大促峰值一到照样顶不住，只是把问题往后拖。
只读副本扇出读、分片拆数据与写，是本题真正把数据库读压力横向摊开的手段。
各实例本地缓存彼此不同步，票状态这类频繁变化的数据会读到过期值，引发错误。
optionExplanations_en: More stateless instances still share one primary; on a cache miss the read storm still hits that single Postgres and saturates its connections.
Vertical scaling has a physical ceiling and stays a single point — a peak still overwhelms it, it just delays the problem.
Read replicas fan out reads and sharding splits data and writes — the actual way to spread the DB read load horizontally here.
Per-instance local caches never sync, so fast-changing data like ticket status is read stale and causes errors.

scenario: 你在面 mid-level（E4）后端，时间有限，防双订这块只来得及落地一种方案。
scenario_en: You are interviewing at mid-level (E4) backend; time is tight and you can only land one no-double-booking approach.
q: mid-level（E4）这题，防双订做到哪种程度就算达标？
q_en: At mid-level (E4), how far must no-double-booking go to clear the bar?
options: 什么都不做，靠数据库唯一约束在写入时报错来兜底就够
预留时给票加 status 字段、设预留超时，再用 cron job 定时清掉过期预留（Good 方案）
必须上 Redis 分布式锁把每次预留串行化，否则高并发下一定双订、达不到及格线
要同时把 OCC、悲观行锁和 Redis 分布式锁这三套并发控制方案都实现出来，好向面试官展示自己掌握得很全面
options_en: Do nothing and rely on a database unique constraint to error out at write time as a fallback.
Give the ticket a status field and a reservation timeout, then run a cron job to clear expired reservations (the Good solution).
You must use a Redis distributed lock, or high concurrency will always double-book and you fail the bar.
Implement OCC, a pessimistic row lock, and a Redis distributed lock all at once to show full mastery.
why: E4 的合格线是 API 和数据模型清晰、能跑通查看和订票，防双订到 Good 方案（status 字段＋超时＋cron）即可，更深属加分。代价：cron 清理有延迟窗口，过期票短暂不可再售。
why_en: The E4 bar is a clear API and data model plus a working view-and-book flow, with no-double-booking at the Good solution (status field, timeout, cron) — anything deeper is bonus. The cost: the cron sweep leaves a lag window where an expired ticket is briefly unsellable.
whenOtherWins: 若同一道题你面的是 senior（E5），就必须落到分布式锁并能讨论 sharding/replication，Good 方案不再够。
tradeoff: 达标所需深度 vs 有限时间的投入

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间表周期性运行的后台任务，这里用来定期扫描并释放已超时的票预留。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cron job is a background task that runs on a fixed schedule, here used to periodically sweep and release expired ticket reservations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 乐观并发控制：写入时用版本号/条件检查判断数据是否被改过，冲突则重试，不预先加锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) checks a version or condition at write time to detect concurrent changes and retries on conflict, without locking up front.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多台服务器协调、保证同一资源同一时刻只被一个请求占用的锁，常用 Redis 实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock coordinates across servers so only one request holds a given resource at a time, often implemented with Redis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读取时就对数据库行加锁、阻止其他事务改动，直到本事务提交，冲突多时更稳但吞吐低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pessimistic row lock locks a database row on read to block other transactions until commit — safer under heavy contention but lower throughput.

optionExplanations: 只靠唯一约束会让用户填完支付才在写入时报错，体验极差，连 Good 方案的预留都没有。
Good 方案用状态字段＋超时＋cron 挡住大多数双订，正是 E4 被期望达到的及格线。
分布式锁是 senior 才被要求的 Great 方案，E4 用 Good 方案已达标，硬上反而超纲费时。
三套并发控制叠在一起既超出 E4 要求，又会吃光有限时间，让基础的 API 和数据模型没做完。
optionExplanations_en: Relying only on the unique constraint errors out at write time after the user has paid — awful UX, and not even the Good solution reservation.
The Good solution status field plus timeout plus cron blocks most double-booking — exactly the pass bar expected at E4.
The distributed lock is the Great solution asked of seniors; E4 already clears the bar with the Good one, so forcing it wastes time.
Stacking three concurrency controls overshoots E4 and burns the limited time, leaving the basic API and data model unfinished.

scenario: 你是 senior（E5）候选人，快速过完高层设计后还剩大半时间用来做 deep dive。
scenario_en: You are a senior (E5) candidate; after quickly clearing the high-level design you have most of the time left for deep dives.
q: senior（E5）这题，必须落到哪些 deep dive 才算达标？（多选）
q_en: At senior (E5), which deep dives must you land to clear the bar?
options: 用 Elasticsearch 等搜索优化引擎支撑事件搜索的低延迟
用分布式锁（或同等质量方案）处理防双订预留
能讨论 sharding 与 replication 等扩展策略（允许在面试官提示下）
把高层设计里的 REST API 重画一遍、力求每个字段都完美
options_en: Use a search-optimized engine like Elasticsearch to give event search low latency.
Handle the no-double-booking reservation with a distributed lock (or an equally strong solution).
Be able to discuss scaling strategies like sharding and replication (interviewer prompting is allowed).
Redraw the high-level design REST API from scratch, chasing perfection on every field.
why: E5 期望约 60% 广度、40% 深度：必须深入 Elasticsearch 搜索、分布式锁防双订，并能讨论 sharding/replication（允许面试官提示）；基础 REST API 应快速带过而非重做。
why_en: E5 expects roughly 60% breadth and 40% depth: go deep on Elasticsearch search and distributed-lock no-double-booking, and be able to discuss sharding and replication (probing is allowed), while breezing through the basic REST API rather than redoing it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于倒排索引的全文搜索引擎，支持按关键词、模糊匹配快速检索，用来替代 SQL 的 LIKE 全表扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is a full-text search engine built on inverted indexes that retrieves by keyword and fuzzy match quickly, replacing SQL LIKE full-table scans.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多台服务器协调、保证同一张票同一时刻只被一个请求预留的锁，常用 Redis 实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock coordinates across servers so a given ticket can only be reserved by one request at a time, often implemented with Redis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分片：按某个键把数据水平切成多份分别存放，拆开单库的数据量与写压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding horizontally splits data by a key into separate partitions to divide a single database data volume and write load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 复制：把主库数据同步到副本节点用于分摊读或高可用，副本会有复制延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication copies primary data to replica nodes to spread reads or provide high availability, with some replication lag.

optionExplanations: 搜索是 E5 明确被要求的深挖点：用搜索优化引擎替掉 LIKE 全表扫描才能满足低延迟。
防双订在 E5 要落到分布式锁这类 Great 方案，而不是 E4 的 Good 方案就收手。
扩展策略要能讨论 sharding 和 replication，即便需要面试官提示也算达标。
基础 REST API 属于该快速带过的广度部分，重画它会挤掉本该用于深挖的时间。
optionExplanations_en: Search is an explicitly expected E5 deep dive: swap LIKE full-table scans for a search-optimized engine to meet low latency.
No-double-booking at E5 must reach a Great solution like a distributed lock, not stop at E4 Good solution.
Scaling strategy must reach a discussion of sharding and replication — clearing the bar even if the interviewer prompts.
The basic REST API is breadth to breeze through; redoing it crowds out the time meant for deep dives.

scenario: 到了 deep dive 阶段，看出并推进设计问题的主导权在候选人和面试官之间的分配随级别不同。
scenario_en: By the deep-dive stage, who spots and drives design problems is split between candidate and interviewer differently depending on level.
q: deep dive 阶段的主导权，随候选人级别该怎么变？
q_en: Who should drive the deep dives as the candidate level rises?
options: 不论什么级别，都应该完全让面试官来驱动，候选人只回答被问到的那部分就好
mid 可以由面试官驱动深挖，senior/staff 必须自己主动看出问题并领跑
不论什么级别，候选人都得从头到尾一个人独自领跑全程，绝不该让面试官插手掌控任何节奏
mid 要主动领跑证明潜力，senior 反而该谦虚地跟着面试官走
options_en: Regardless of level, let the interviewer drive and the candidate only answers what is asked.
At mid-level the interviewer may drive the deep dives, but senior/staff must proactively spot problems and lead.
Regardless of level, the candidate must lead alone throughout and not let the interviewer set the pace.
Mid-level should lead to prove potential, while seniors should humbly follow the interviewer instead.
why: 级别越高，期望的主动性（agency）越强：mid 允许面试官接手后段深挖，senior/staff 必须自己看出瓶颈并领跑，否则会被读作深度和担当都不足。
why_en: The higher the level, the more agency is expected: at mid-level the interviewer may take over the later deep dives, while senior/staff must spot the bottlenecks and lead, or it reads as lacking depth and drive.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确表示要自己把控节奏（如时间紧、需要聚焦某一点），即便是 staff 也应配合让位，不要硬抢主导。
tradeoff: 候选人主导 vs 面试官主导（随级别调）

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动性/自主性：候选人不等提示就自己看出问题、提出改进并推进设计的能力，级别越高要求越强。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Agency is the candidate proactivity — spotting problems, proposing improvements, and driving the design without being prompted — expected more at higher levels.

optionExplanations: 全程被动只在 mid 可接受；senior/staff 这样做会显得看不出问题、缺乏主动性。
mid 期望广度、允许面试官驱动后段；senior/staff 期望主动看出瓶颈并领跑，这正是级别差别。
全程硬抢、不让面试官引导，会错过对方想聚焦的重点，反而显得不会读场。
级别与主动性的关系被弄反了：越高级越该主动，而不是越高级越退让。
optionExplanations_en: Being passive throughout is only acceptable at mid-level; at senior/staff it reads as failing to spot problems and lacking proactivity.
Mid-level expects breadth and lets the interviewer drive the tail; senior/staff are expected to spot bottlenecks and lead — that is the level difference.
Leading hard the whole time and blocking the interviewer steering misses what they want to focus on and reads as poor room-reading.
This inverts level and proactivity: higher levels should be more proactive, not more deferential.
